# Linked profile access to protected routes (2026-01-31 16:33Z)

_**User**_

I would like to add a new restriction for authenticated users.

Only the users that have a linked profile will be able to access /protected. Otherwise they will be redirected to page Which tells them they need an admin to approve their email address

Enforce this on the server for all endpoints except / and /auth and static (the way it's setup already. Just add it to that)

Keep it simple stupid and dry

Make sure the middleware handles everything not the client (proxy.ts)

        "contents": "import { EnvVarWarning } from \"@/components/env-var-warning\";\nimport { AuthButton } from \"@/components/auth-button\";\nimport { ThemeSwitcher } from \"@/components/theme-switcher\";\nimport Link from \"next/link\";\nimport { Suspense } from \"react\";\nimport { createClient } from \"@/lib/supabase/server\";\nimport { redirect } from \"next/navigation\";\nimport { hasEmailIdentity } from \"@/lib/auth-helpers\";\n\nexport default async function ProtectedLayout({\n  children,\n}: {\n  children: React.ReactNode;\n}) {\n  const supabase = await createClient();\n  const { data } = await supabase.auth.getClaims();\n\n  // Redirect to login if not authenticated\n  if (!data?.claims) {\n    redirect(\"/auth/login\");\n  }\n\n  // Redirect to verify email if no email identity linked\n  const hasEmail = await hasEmailIdentity();\n  if (!hasEmail) {\n    redirect(\"/auth/verify-email\");\n  }\n\n  return (\n    &lt;main className=\"min-h-screen flex flex-col items-center\"&gt;\n      &lt;div className=\"flex-1 w-full flex flex-col gap-20 items-center\"&gt;\n        &lt;nav className=\"w-full flex justify-center border-b border-b-foreground/10 h-16\"&gt;\n          &lt;div className=\"w-full max-w-5xl flex justify-between items-center p-3 px-5 text-sm\"&gt;\n            &lt;div className=\"flex gap-5 items-center font-semibold\"&gt;\n              &lt;Link href={\"/\"}&gt;Next.js Supabase Starter&lt;/Link&gt;\n}",

        "contents": "import { NextResponse, type NextRequest } from \"next/server\";\n\nexport async function updateSession(request: NextRequest) {\n  let supabaseResponse = NextResponse.next({\n    request,\n  });\n\n  // If the env vars are not set, skip proxy check. You can remove this\n  // once you setup the project.\n\n  // With Fluid compute, don't put this client in a global environment\n  // variable. Always create a new one on each request.\n  const supabase = createServerClient(\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL!,\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY!,\n    {\n      cookies: {\n        getAll() {\n          return request.cookies.getAll();\n        },\n        setAll(cookiesToSet) {\n          cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value }) =&gt;\n            request.cookies.set(name, value),\n          );\n          supabaseResponse = NextResponse.next({\n            request,\n          });\n          cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value, options }) =&gt;\n            supabaseResponse.cookies.set(name, value, options),\n          );\n        },\n      },\n    },\n  );\n\n  // Do not run code between createServerClient and\n  // supabase.auth.getClaims(). A simple mistake could make it very hard to debug\n  // issues with users being randomly logged out.\n\n  // IMPORTANT: If you remove getClaims() and you use server-side rendering\n  // with the Supabase client, your users may be randomly logged out.\n  const { data } = await supabase.auth.getClaims();\n  const user = data?.claims;\n\n  if (\n    request.nextUrl.pathname !== \"/\" &amp;&amp;\n    !user &amp;&amp;\n    !request.nextUrl.pathname.startsWith(\"/login\") &amp;&amp;\n}",

        "contents": "await supabase\n  .from('profiles')\n  .update({ \n    user_id: user.id,\n    picture: user.user_metadata.avatar_url  // Default to Google picture\n  })\n  .eq('work_email', workEmail);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Step 4: Middleware Validation\n\nQuery database for profile linked to current auth.user and check &#96;removed_access IS NULL&#96; on every request to protected routes.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// Middleware check\nconst { data: profile } = await supabase\n  .from('profiles')\n  .select('id, role, removed_access')\n  .eq('user_id', user.id)\n  .single();\n\nif (!profile) redirect('/auth/verify-work-email');\nif (profile.removed_access) redirect('/auth/access-revoked');\n// User has active access, continue...\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Estimated Complexity\n\n| Task | Complexity | Lines of Code |\n\n|------|------------|---------------|\n\n| Delete old auth files | Trivial | -500 lines |\n\n| Security lockdown config | Trivial | ~20 lines TOML |\n\n| Database migration | Low | ~40 lines SQL (users, profiles, indexes) |\n\n| Constants + validation | Trivial | ~25 lines |\n\n| Server actions (auth logic) | Medium | ~60 lines |\n\n| Middleware update | Medium | ~50 lines (includes DB queries) |\n\n| Google login page | Low | ~30 lines |\n\n| Work email form + linking | Medium | ~120 lines |\n\n| Pending approval page | Low | ~20 lines |\n\n| Access revoked page | Low | ~20 lines |\n\n**Total new code**: ~385 lines (vs ~500 lines deleted)\n\n## Separation of Concerns\n\n### Supabase (Auth + Storage Only)\n\n- **Authentication**: Google OAuth flow, session management, OTP emails\n- **Database**: Store profiles and users data (no RLS - Next.js handles access control)\n- **No business logic**: No custom hooks, no stored procedures, no triggers, no functions\n\n### Next.js (All Business Logic)\n\n- **Middleware**: Profile verification, access checks, role-based routing\n- **Server Actions**: Profile linking, access revocation\n- **Validation**: Domain validation, input sanitization, business rules\n- **Authorization**: Role hierarchy checks, permission enforcement\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                         Next.js                                  │",

        "contents": "   - No Row Level Security policies\n   - No database triggers or functions\n   - All access control handled by Next.js\n\n### Next.js (Application Layer - All Business Logic)\n\n1. **Middleware Verification**:\n\n   - Queries &#96;profiles&#96; table for linked user_id\n   - Checks &#96;removed_access&#96; is null for active access\n   - Enforces role-based route protection\n   - Real-time verification (instant access revocation)\n\n2. **Domain Validation** (in server actions):\n\n   - Client-side validation for UX (immediate feedback)\n   - Server-side validation before sending OTP\n   - Validates email format and CZU domain\n\n3. **Access Management** (in server actions):\n\n   - Admin sets &#96;removed_access&#96; timestamp and &#96;removed_access_by&#96; profile\n   - Immediate effect on next request\n   - Audit trail of who revoked access and when\n\n## Authentication Flow Details\n\n### Step 1: Google Login\n\nUser clicks Google login button, Supabase handles OAuth flow.\n\n### Step 2: Work Email Input with Domain Validation\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// Validate domain before sending OTP\nif (!isValidWorkEmailDomain(workEmail)) {\n  throw new Error('Email must be @studenti.czu.cz or @pef.czu.cz');\n}\n\n// Send OTP to work email (only after domain validation passes)\nconst { error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithOtp({\n  email: workEmail,\n  options: { shouldCreateUser: false }\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Step 3: OTP Verification and Profile Linking\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// After user enters OTP, verify it\nconst { error } = await supabase.auth.verifyOtp({\n  email: workEmail,\n  token: otpCode,\n  type: 'email'\n});\n\n// Check if profile exists for this work email\nconst { data: profile } = await supabase\n  .from('profiles')\n  .select('id')\n  .eq('work_email', workEmail)\n  .single();\n\nif (!profile) {\n  // No profile exists - redirect to pending approval\n  redirect('/auth/pending-approval');\n}\n\n// Link profile to current user\nconst { data: { user } } = await supabase.auth.getUser();\nawait supabase\n  .from('profiles')\n  .update({ \n    user_id: user.id,",

        "contents": "import { redirect } from \"next/navigation\";\nimport { type NextRequest } from \"next/server\";\n\nimport { hasEmailIdentity } from \"@/lib/auth-helpers\";\n\n/**\n * Handles OAuth callback from Google\n * Exchanges the code for a session and redirects appropriately\n */\nexport async function GET(request: NextRequest) {\n  const { searchParams, origin } = new URL(request.url);\n  const code = searchParams.get(\"code\");\n  const next = searchParams.get(\"next\");\n\n  if (code) {\n    const supabase = await createClient();\n    const { error } = await supabase.auth.exchangeCodeForSession(code);\n\n    if (!error) {\n      // Check if user has email identity linked\n      // If not, redirect to verify-email page\n      const hasEmail = await hasEmailIdentity();\n      const redirectTo = next || (hasEmail ? \"/protected\" : \"/auth/verify-email\");\n      redirect(redirectTo);\n    }\n  }\n\n  // Redirect to error page if something went wrong\n  redirect(&#96;/auth/error?error=Failed to authenticate with Google&#96;);\n}",

        "contents": "## Architecture Overview\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart TD\n    subgraph auth_flow [Authentication Flow]\n        A[User clicks Google Login] --&gt; B[Google OAuth]\n        B --&gt; C[Redirect back with Google identity]\n        C --&gt; D{Profile linked to user?}\n        D --&gt;|No| E[Prompt for work email]\n        E --&gt; F{Domain is czu.cz?}\n        F --&gt;|No| G[Show domain error]\n        G --&gt; E\n        F --&gt;|Yes| H[Send OTP to work email]\n        H --&gt; I[User enters OTP]\n        I --&gt; J{Profile exists for work email?}\n        J --&gt;|No| K[Pending Approval Page]\n        J --&gt;|Yes| L[Link profile to user]\n        D --&gt;|Yes| M{Access revoked?}\n        L --&gt; M\n        M --&gt;|Yes| N[Show access revoked]\n        M --&gt;|No| O[Grant Full Access]\n    end\n\n    subgraph request_flow [Request Validation]\n        P[Incoming Request] --&gt; Q[Middleware queries database]\n        Q --&gt; R{Profile linked to user?}\n        R --&gt;|No| S[Redirect to verify email]\n        R --&gt;|Yes| T{removed_access is null?}\n        T --&gt;|No| U[Show access revoked]\n        T --&gt;|Yes| V[Allow access]\n    end\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Validation Flow\n\n**Two-stage validation:**\n\n1. **Before OTP (Domain Check)**: Validate email ends with &#96;@studenti.czu.cz&#96; or &#96;@pef.czu.cz&#96;\n\n   - Client-side: Immediate feedback\n   - Server-side: Validated before &#96;signInWithOtp&#96; is called\n\n2. **After OTP (Profile Linking)**: Check if a profile exists for the verified work email\n\n   - If profile exists with that work_email → link profile to auth.user\n   - If no profile exists → show \"Pending Approval\" (admin must create profile first)\n   - Checked on every request via middleware\n\n## Database Schema (Supabase Migrations)\n\nTwo tables with **no RLS** - all access control is handled in Next.js:\n\n1. **&#96;users&#96;** - Custom table to sync with auth.users (Google OAuth), synced via Next.js server actions\n2. **&#96;profiles&#96;** - User authentication profile data with role and access control\n\n**Important**: No Supabase functions, triggers, or RLS policies. All business logic lives in Next.js.\n\nUse MODDATETIME extension to set the &#96;updated_at&#96; column on every update.",

        "detailedLines": [
          {

          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 40
          },

            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid",

          },

          {
            "text": "        A[User clicks Google Login] --&gt; B[Google OAuth]",
            "lineNumber": 44
          },
          {
            "text": "        B --&gt; C[Redirect back with Google identity]",
            "lineNumber": 45
          },
          {
            "text": "        C --&gt; D{Profile linked to user?}",
            "lineNumber": 46
          },
          {
            "text": "        D --&gt;|No| E[Prompt for work email]",
            "lineNumber": 47
          },
          {
            "text": "        E --&gt; F{Domain is czu.cz?}",
            "lineNumber": 48
          },
          {
            "text": "        F --&gt;|No| G[Show domain error]",
            "lineNumber": 49
          },
          {
            "text": "        G --&gt; E",
            "lineNumber": 50
          },
          {
            "text": "        F --&gt;|Yes| H[Send OTP to work email]",
            "lineNumber": 51
          },
          {
            "text": "        H --&gt; I[User enters OTP]",
            "lineNumber": 52
          },
          {
            "text": "        I --&gt; J{Profile exists for work email?}",
            "lineNumber": 53
          },
          {
            "text": "        J --&gt;|No| K[Pending Approval Page]",
            "lineNumber": 54
          },
          {
            "text": "        J --&gt;|Yes| L[Link profile to user]",
            "lineNumber": 55
          },
          {
            "text": "        D --&gt;|Yes| M{Access revoked?}",
            "lineNumber": 56
          },
          {
            "text": "        L --&gt; M",
            "lineNumber": 57
          },
          {
            "text": "        M --&gt;|Yes| N[Show access revoked]",
            "lineNumber": 58
          },
          {
            "text": "        M --&gt;|No| O[Grant Full Access]",
            "lineNumber": 59
          },
          {
            "text": "    end",
            "lineNumber": 60
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 61
          },
          {
            "text": "    subgraph request_flow [Request Validation]",
            "lineNumber": 62
          },
          {
            "text": "        P[Incoming Request] --&gt; Q[Middleware queries database]",
            "lineNumber": 63
          },
          {
            "text": "        Q --&gt; R{Profile linked to user?}",
            "lineNumber": 64
          },
          {
            "text": "        R --&gt;|No| S[Redirect to verify email]",
            "lineNumber": 65
          },
          {
            "text": "        R --&gt;|Yes| T{removed_access is null?}",
            "lineNumber": 66
          },
          {
            "text": "        T --&gt;|No| U[Show access revoked]",
            "lineNumber": 67
          },
          {
            "text": "        T --&gt;|Yes| V[Allow access]",
            "lineNumber": 68
          },
          {
            "text": "    end",
            "lineNumber": 69
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 70
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 71
          },
          {
            "text": "## Validation Flow",
            "lineNumber": 72
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 73
          },
          {
            "text": "**Two-stage validation:**",
            "lineNumber": 74
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 75
          },
          {
            "text": "1. **Before OTP (Domain Check)**: Validate email ends with &#96;@studenti.czu.cz&#96; or &#96;@pef.czu.cz&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 76
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 77
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Client-side: Immediate feedback",
            "lineNumber": 78
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Server-side: Validated before &#96;signInWithOtp&#96; is called",
            "lineNumber": 79
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 80
          },
          {
            "text": "2. **After OTP (Profile Linking)**: Check if a profile exists for the verified work email",
            "lineNumber": 81
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 82
          },
          {
            "text": "   - If profile exists with that work_email → link profile to auth.user",
            "lineNumber": 83
          },
          {
            "text": "   - If no profile exists → show \"Pending Approval\" (admin must create profile first)",
            "lineNumber": 84
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Checked on every request via middleware",
            "lineNumber": 85
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 86
          },
          {
            "text": "## Database Schema (Supabase Migrations)",
            "lineNumber": 87
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 88
          },
          {
            "text": "Two tables with **no RLS** - all access control is handled in Next.js:",
            "lineNumber": 89
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 90
          },
          {
            "text": "1. **&#96;users&#96;** - Custom table to sync with auth.users (Google OAuth), synced via Next.js server actions",
            "lineNumber": 91
          },
          {
            "text": "2. **&#96;profiles&#96;** - User authentication profile data with role and access control",
            "lineNumber": 92
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 93
          },
          {
            "text": "**Important**: No Supabase functions, triggers, or RLS policies. All business logic lives in Next.js.",
            "lineNumber": 94
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 95
          },
          {
            "text": "Use MODDATETIME extension to set the &#96;updated_at&#96; column on every update.",
            "lineNumber": 96
          }
        ]
      },
      "score": 0.32285061478614807
    },

        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./.cursor/plans/work_email_auth_system_467a2b18.plan.md",

        "contents": "## Supabase Configuration Changes\n\nUpdate [&#96;supabase/config.toml&#96;](supabase/config.toml):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;toml\n[auth]\nenable_manual_linking = true        # Required for work email linking\nenable_anonymous_sign_ins = false   # Block anonymous access\n\n[auth.email]\nenable_signup = false               # Block direct email/password signup\nenable_confirmations = false        # We use OTP for work email, not signup confirmation\n\n[auth.external.google]\nenabled = true\nclient_id = \"env(GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID)\"\nsecret = \"env(GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET)\"\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Profile Verification (Next.js Middleware)\n\nAll verification logic lives in Next.js middleware, not in Supabase:\n\n- **Profile Linked**: Check &#96;profiles.user_id&#96; matches current auth.user.id\n- **Access Active**: Check &#96;profiles.removed_access IS NULL&#96;\n- **User Role**: Read &#96;profiles.role&#96; column (student, team_leader, coach, admin)\n\nThis approach:\n\n- Keeps all business logic in Next.js (single source of truth)\n- Allows real-time updates (e.g., instant access revocation)\n- Admin pre-creates profiles, users link via work email verification\n- Supabase only handles auth + data storage (no custom hooks or functions)\n\n## Development &amp; Testing with Supabase MCP\n\nThe project has a &#96;supabase/&#96; directory with Supabase MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration available for:\n\n1. **Running migrations**: Apply and test database schema changes locally\n2. **Debugging auth flow**: Inspect user sessions and profile data\n3. **Testing verification logic**: Query profiles table for auth checks\n\n**Useful MCP commands for development:**\n\n- Seed test data into profiles table for auth testing\n- Inspect auth.users and profiles tables\n- Test profile linking and access revocation queries\n\n## Key Security Features\n\n### Supabase (Data Layer Only)\n\n1. **Database Constraints**:\n\n   - Domain constraint ensures only valid CZU domains in profiles\n   - Unique constraints on work_email, user_id\n\n2. **No RLS or Functions**:\n\n   - No Row Level Security policies\n   - No database triggers or functions",

        "contents": "import { redirect } from \"next/navigation\";\nimport { VerifyEmailForm } from \"@/components/verify-email-form\";\nimport { hasEmailIdentity } from \"@/lib/auth-helpers\";\n\n/**\n * Email verification page\n * Users must link an email via OTP to their Google OAuth account\n */\nexport default async function VerifyEmailPage() {\n  const supabase = await createClient();\n  const { data } = await supabase.auth.getClaims();\n\n  // Redirect to login if not authenticated\n  if (!data?.claims) {\n    redirect(\"/auth/login\");\n  }\n\n  // Redirect to protected if already has email identity\n  const hasEmail = await hasEmailIdentity();\n  if (hasEmail) {\n    redirect(\"/protected\");\n  }\n\n  return (\n    &lt;div className=\"flex min-h-svh w-full items-center justify-center p-6 md:p-10\"&gt;\n      &lt;div className=\"w-full max-w-sm\"&gt;\n        &lt;VerifyEmailForm /&gt;\n      &lt;/div&gt;\n    &lt;/div&gt;\n  );\n}",

        "contents": "### ORM Best Practices\n\n- Use type-safe ORMs (Drizzle, Prisma, etc.)\n- Define schemas with proper relationships and constraints\n- Infer types from schema definitions\n- Write repository-style helpers to isolate queries\n- Implement proper migrations\n\n### Data Access Patterns\n\n- Keep database queries in dedicated modules\n- Avoid N+1 queries; use joins and CTEs\n- Implement pagination for list endpoints\n- Use select projections to limit payload size\n\n## Authentication &amp; Authorization\n\n- Implement server-side auth checks\n- Never trust client-side auth flags\n- Use middleware for route protection\n- Store user data securely with proper encryption\n\n## Testing Strategy\n\n### Unit Testing (Vitest)\n\n- **Never mock internal code** - only mock external dependencies\n- Use MSW for API mocking when needed\n- Test utilities, repositories, and business logic\n- Mock external services (APIs, databases, file systems)\n\n### Component Testing (React Testing Library)\n\n- Test interactive components with proper accessibility\n- Ensure loading and error states are covered\n- Test user interactions and state changes\n- Use data-testid sparingly; prefer semantic queries\n\n### Integration Testing\n\n- Test API endpoints with real database connections\n- Use test databases with proper cleanup\n- Test authentication flows end-to-end\n- Mock external services consistently\n\n### Test Structure\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// Example test structure\ndescribe(\"Feature\", () =&gt; {\n  describe(\"when condition\", () =&gt; {\n    it(\"should expected behavior\", async () =&gt; {\n      // Arrange\n      // Act\n      // Assert\n    });\n  });\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Error Handling &amp; Observability\n\n- Implement early returns on invalid input (fail fast)\n- Use typed error codes and messages\n- Log server-side with contextual metadata\n- Never expose stack traces to clients\n- Provide user-friendly error messages\n\n## Security Best Practices\n\n- Validate all inputs at boundaries\n- Use environment variables for sensitive data (server-only)\n- Implement proper CORS policies\n- Sanitize user inputs\n- Use HTTPS in production\n- Implement rate limiting where appropriate",

        "contents": "for select\nto authenticated\nusing ( (select auth.uid()) = auth_user_id );\n\n-- Users can update their own user record\ncreate policy \"Users can update their own user record\" on public.users\nfor update\nto authenticated\nusing ( (select auth.uid()) = auth_user_id )\nwith check ( (select auth.uid()) = auth_user_id );\n\n-- Users can insert their own user record (during signup via trigger)\ncreate policy \"Users can insert their own user record\" on public.users\nfor insert\nto authenticated\nwith check ( (select auth.uid()) = auth_user_id );\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- RLS POLICIES - PROFILES TABLE\n-- ============================================================================\n\n-- Users can view their own profile\ncreate policy \"Users can view their own profile\" on public.profiles\nfor select\nto authenticated\nusing (\n  user_id in (\n    select id\n    from public.users\n    where auth_user_id = (select auth.uid())\n  )\n);\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- RLS POLICIES - REALTIME MESSAGES TABLE\n-- ============================================================================\n\n-- Users can receive broadcasts for their own user record\ncreate policy \"Users can receive broadcasts for their own user record\" on realtime.messages\nfor select\nto authenticated\nusing (\n  topic like 'users:%'\n  and exists (\n    select 1\n    from public.users\n    where auth_user_id = (select auth.uid())\n    and topic = 'users:' || id::text\n  )\n);\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- GRANTS\n-- ============================================================================\n\n-- Grant execute permissions for trigger functions\ngrant execute on function public.handle_new_auth_user() to authenticated;\ngrant execute on function public.handle_new_auth_user() to anon;\ngrant execute on function public.validate_czu_email_domain_trigger() to authenticated;\ngrant execute on function public.validate_czu_email_domain_trigger() to anon;\ngrant execute on function public.before_user_created_hook(jsonb) to authenticated;",

        "contents": "export function VerifyEmailForm() {\nconst handleSendOTP = async \n\n    }\n  };\n\n  /**\n   * Verifies the OTP code and links email identity to user\n   * Uses type 'email_change' since we're updating the user's email via updateUser()\n   * With enable_manual_linking = true, this will link the email identity\n   * to the existing authenticated user account\n   */\n  const verifyOTP = useCallback(async () =&gt; {\n    setError(null);\n    setIsLoading(true);\n\n    try {\n      // Verify OTP code for email change/linking\n      // Use type 'email_change' because we used updateUser() to initiate the flow\n      // With enable_manual_linking = true, this will link the email identity\n      // to the current authenticated user instead of creating a new user\n      const { error: verifyError } = await supabase.auth.verifyOtp({\n        email: email.trim(),\n        token: otpCode.trim(),\n        type: \"email_change\",\n      });\n\n      if (verifyError) {\n        setError(verifyError.message || \"Invalid OTP code\");\n        setIsLoading(false);\n        return;\n      }\n\n      // Refresh session to ensure identities are updated\n      await supabase.auth.refreshSession();\n\n      // Clear persisted state on success\n      clearPersistedState();\n\n      // Success - redirect to protected page\n      router.push(\"/protected\");\n      router.refresh();\n    } catch (err) {\n      setError(\"An unexpected error occurred\");\n      setIsLoading(false);\n    }\n  }, [email, otpCode, supabase, router]);\n\n  /**\n   * Handles form submission for OTP verification\n   */\n  const handleVerifyOTP = async (e: React.FormEvent) =&gt; {\n    e.preventDefault();\n    await verifyOTP();\n  };\n\n  /**\n   * Loads persisted state from sessionStorage after component mounts (client-side only)\n   * This prevents hydration mismatches between server and client\n   */\n}",

        "contents": "import { cookies } from \"next/headers\";\n\n/**\n * Especially important if using Fluid compute: Don't put this client in a\n * global variable. Always create a new client within each function when using\n * it.\n */\nexport async function createClient() {\n  const cookieStore = await cookies();\n\n  return createServerClient(\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL!,\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY!,\n    {\n      cookies: {\n        getAll() {\n          return cookieStore.getAll();\n        },\n        setAll(cookiesToSet) {\n          try {\n            cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value, options }) =&gt;\n              cookieStore.set(name, value, options),\n            );\n          } catch {\n            // The &#96;setAll&#96; method was called from a Server Component.\n            // This can be ignored if you have proxy refreshing\n            // user sessions.\n          }\n        },\n      },\n    },\n  );\n}",

        "contents": "└─ e2e/                       # End-to-end tests\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Directory Conventions\n\n- Use **kebab-case** for folders and files\n- Co-locate tests next to source: &#96;*.test.ts(x)&#96;\n- Export from &#96;index.ts&#96; barrels only when it helps DX without circular deps\n\n## Next.js App Router Rules\n\n### Server vs Client Components\n\n- **Default to RSC** (no \"use client\"). Use client components only for:\n  - Interactivity (event handlers)\n  - Browser APIs (localStorage, window, etc.)\n  - Third-party libraries requiring client-side initialization\n\n### Server Boundaries\n\n- Keep data access in server context (RSC, server actions, API routes)\n- API routes in &#96;app/api&#96; are for external webhooks only\n- Use internal APIs (tRPC, server actions) for app-to-app communication\n\n### Performance &amp; UX\n\n- Use &#96;&lt;Suspense&gt;&#96; for async UI; provide skeletons\n- Implement proper loading and error boundaries\n- Use Next.js caching (&#96;revalidateTag&#96;, &#96;revalidatePath&#96;) appropriately\n- Prefer Edge runtime for simple operations, Node for complex ones\n\n### Accessibility\n\n- All interactive elements must have proper roles and labels\n- Ensure keyboard navigation support\n- Provide ARIA attributes where needed\n- Test with screen readers\n\n## API Architecture\n\n### Internal APIs (tRPC Recommended)\n\n- Organize by feature domains\n- Use Zod for input validation\n- Implement proper error handling with custom error classes\n- Keep business logic server-side (no JSX in API layer)\n- Write integration tests with mocked external services\n- **Router logic should be application code only** - delegate to business logic services\n- **Use only protected procedures** for all endpoints\n- **Split procedures and routers** into separate files for better organization\n\n### Application Logic vs Business Logic\n\n**Application Logic** (in tRPC procedures):\n- Input validation and sanitization\n- Authentication and authorization checks\n- Request/response formatting\n- Error handling and mapping\n- Delegation to business logic services\n- Logging and observability",

          {
            "lineNumber": 74
          },
          {
            "text": "- Use &#96;&lt;Suspense&gt;&#96; for async UI; provide skeletons",
            "lineNumber": 75
          },
          {
            "text": "- Implement proper loading and error boundaries",
            "lineNumber": 76
          },
          {
            "text": "- Use Next.js caching (&#96;revalidateTag&#96;, &#96;revalidatePath&#96;) appropriately",
            "lineNumber": 77
          },
          {
            "text": "- Prefer Edge runtime for simple operations, Node for complex ones",
            "lineNumber": 78
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 79
          },
          {
            "text": "### Accessibility",
            "lineNumber": 80
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 81
          },
          {
            "text": "- All interactive elements must have proper roles and labels",
            "lineNumber": 82
          },
          {
            "text": "- Ensure keyboard navigation support",
            "lineNumber": 83
          },
          {
            "text": "- Provide ARIA attributes where needed",
            "lineNumber": 84
          },
          {
            "text": "- Test with screen readers",
            "lineNumber": 85
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 86
          },
          {
            "text": "## API Architecture",
            "lineNumber": 87
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 88
          },
          {
            "text": "### Internal APIs (tRPC Recommended)",
            "lineNumber": 89
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 90
          },
          {
            "text": "- Organize by feature domains",
            "lineNumber": 91
          },
          {
            "text": "- Use Zod for input validation",
            "lineNumber": 92
          },
          {
            "text": "- Implement proper error handling with custom error classes",
            "lineNumber": 93
          },
          {
            "text": "- Keep business logic server-side (no JSX in API layer)",
            "lineNumber": 94
          },
          {
            "text": "- Write integration tests with mocked external services",
            "lineNumber": 95
          },
          {
            "text": "- **Router logic should be application code only** - delegate to business logic services",
            "lineNumber": 96
          },
          {
            "text": "- **Use only protected procedures** for all endpoints",
            "lineNumber": 97
          },
          {
            "text": "- **Split procedures and routers** into separate files for better organization",
            "lineNumber": 98
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 99
          },
          {
            "text": "### Application Logic vs Business Logic",
            "lineNumber": 100
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 101
          },
          {
            "text": "**Application Logic** (in tRPC procedures):",
            "lineNumber": 102
          },
          {
            "text": "- Input validation and sanitization",
            "lineNumber": 103
          },
          {
            "text": "- Authentication and authorization checks",
            "lineNumber": 104
          },
          {
            "text": "- Request/response formatting",
            "lineNumber": 105
          },
          {
            "text": "- Error handling and mapping",
            "lineNumber": 106
          },
          {
            "text": "- Delegation to business logic services",
            "lineNumber": 107
          },
          {
            "text": "- Logging and observability",
            "lineNumber": 108
          }
        ]
      },

{\n    try {\n      const result = await performFeatureAction({\n        userId: ctx.auth.userId,\n        ...input\n      });\n      \n      return { success: true, data: result };\n    } catch (error) {\n      if (error instanceof CustomError) {\n        throw error;\n      }\n      throw new CustomError(\"INTERNAL_ERROR\", \"An unexpected error occurred\");\n    }\n  });\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### tRPC Router Template\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// src/server/api/routers/[feature].ts\nimport { createTRPCRouter } from \"../trpc\";\nimport { actionProcedure } from \"../procedures/[feature]\";\n\nexport const featureRouter = createTRPCRouter({\n  action: actionProcedure,\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Custom Error Template\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// src/lib/errors.ts\nexport class CustomError extends Error {\n  constructor(\n    public code: string,\n    message: string,\n    public statusCode: number = 500\n  ) {\n    super(message);\n    this.name = \"CustomError\";\n  }\n}\n\nexport const createCustomError = (code: string, message: string, statusCode?: number) =&gt;         "contents": "comment on function public.handle_user_update_restriction() is 'Trigger function that restricts user updates to suggested_work_email only. Automatically updates last_otp_sent_at when suggested_work_email changes. Prevents modification of all other fields including google_email, google_profile_picture, google_full_name, auth_user_id, id, and created_at.';\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- TRIGGERS\n-- ============================================================================\n\n-- Create trigger to enforce update restrictions on users table\n-- This trigger runs BEFORE the update to prevent field modifications\ndrop trigger if exists users_update_restriction_trigger on public.users;\n\ncreate trigger users_update_restriction_trigger\nbefore update on public.users\nfor each row\nexecute function public.handle_user_update_restriction();\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- RLS POLICIES\n-- ============================================================================\n\n-- Drop the existing permissive update policy\ndrop policy if exists \"Users can update their own user record\" on public.users;\n\n-- Create a new restrictive update policy that only allows updating suggested_work_email\n-- The trigger function will enforce that only suggested_work_email can be changed\ncreate policy \"Users can update only suggested_work_email\" on public.users\nfor update\nto authenticated\nusing ( (select auth.uid()) = auth_user_id )\nwith check ( (select auth.uid()) = auth_user_id );\n\ncomment on policy \"Users can update only suggested_work_email\" on public.users is 'RLS policy that allows authenticated users to update only their own user record. The handle_user_update_restriction() trigger enforces that only suggested_work_email can be modified, and automatically updates last_otp_sent_at.';\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- GRANTS\n-- ============================================================================\n\n-- Grant execute permissions for the new trigger function",
        "signatures": {},

        "contents": "- &#96;anon&#96;: an unauthenticated request (the user is not logged in)\n- &#96;authenticated&#96;: an authenticated request (the user is logged in)\n\nThese are actually [Postgres Roles](mdc:docs/guides/database/postgres/roles). You can use these roles within your Policies using the &#96;TO&#96; clause:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Profiles are viewable by everyone\"\non profiles\nfor select\nto authenticated, anon\nusing ( true );\n\n-- OR\n\ncreate policy \"Public profiles are viewable only by authenticated users\"\non profiles\nfor select\nto authenticated\nusing ( true );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nNote that &#96;for ...&#96; must be added after the table but before the roles. &#96;to ...&#96; must be added after &#96;for ...&#96;:\n\n### Incorrect\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Public profiles are viewable only by authenticated users\"\non profiles\nto authenticated\nfor select\nusing ( true );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Correct\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Public profiles are viewable only by authenticated users\"\non profiles\nfor select\nto authenticated\nusing ( true );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Multiple operations\n\nPostgreSQL policies do not support specifying multiple operations in a single FOR clause. You need to create separate policies for each operation.\n\n### Incorrect\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Profiles can be created and deleted by any user\"\non profiles\nfor insert, delete -- cannot create a policy on multiple operators\nto authenticated\nwith check ( true )\nusing ( true );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Correct\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Profiles can be created by any user\"\non profiles\nfor insert\nto authenticated\nwith check ( true );\n\ncreate policy \"Profiles can be deleted by any user\"\non profiles\nfor delete\nto authenticated\nusing ( true );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Helper functions\n\nSupabase provides some helper functions that make it easier to write Policies.\n\n### &#96;auth.uid()&#96;\n\nReturns the ID of the user making the request.\n\n### &#96;auth.jwt()&#96;\n\nReturns the JWT of the user making the request. Anything that you store in the user's &#96;raw_app_meta_data&#96; column or the &#96;raw_user_meta_data&#96; column will be accessible using this function. It's important to know the distinction between these two:\n\n- &#96;raw_user_meta_data&#96; - can be updated by the authenticated user using the &#96;supabase.auth.update()&#96; function. It is not a good place to store authorization data.",

          {

        "contents": "Use MODDATETIME extension to set the &#96;updated_at&#96; column on every update.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\n-- Users table to sync with auth.users (Google OAuth)\n-- Note: Synced via Next.js server actions, not database triggers\ncreate table public.users (\n  id uuid primary key references auth.users(id) on delete cascade,\n  email text not null,\n  name text,\n  picture text,\n  created_at timestamptz default now() not null,\n  updated_at timestamptz default now() not null\n);\n\n-- Role enum for profiles (authorization)\ncreate type public.profile_role as enum ('student', 'team_leader', 'coach', 'admin');\n\n-- Profiles table (pre-created by admin, linked to user after verification)\n-- Focus: Authentication and authorization only\ncreate table public.profiles (\n  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),\n  name text not null,\n  user_id uuid unique references public.users(id) on delete set null,  -- linked after OTP verification\n  work_email text unique not null,\n  role public.profile_role not null default 'student',\n  removed_access timestamptz,  -- null = active, set = revoked\n  removed_access_by uuid references public.profiles(id) on delete set null,\n  created_at timestamptz default now() not null,\n  updated_at timestamptz default now() not null,\n  constraint valid_czu_domain check (\n    work_email like '%@studenti.czu.cz' or work_email like '%@pef.czu.cz'\n  )\n);\n\n-- Indexes for auth queries\ncreate index profiles_user_id_idx on public.profiles(user_id);\ncreate index profiles_work_email_idx on public.profiles(work_email);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Entity Relationships\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n┌─────────────────┐       ┌─────────────────┐\n│   auth.users    │       │    profiles     │\n│  (Supabase)     │       │  (Auth only)    │\n├─────────────────┤       ├─────────────────┤\n│ id (uuid)       │◄──┐   │ id (uuid)       │\n│ email (google)  │   │   │ name            │\n│ ...auth fields  │   └───│ user_id (1:1)   │",

          },
          {

          },
          {
            "text": "  role public.profile_role not null default 'student',",

          },
          {
            "text": "  removed_access_by uuid references public.profiles(id) on delete set null,",

          },
          {
            "text": "  created_at timestamptz default now() not null,",

          },
          {
            "text": "  updated_at timestamptz default now() not null,",

          },
          {

        "contents": "comment on function public.link_user_to_profile() is 'Trigger function that automatically links profile rows to user rows when auth.users.email matches profiles.work_email. Matches based on currently logged in user email (auth.users.email), uid in user table row (public.users.auth_user_id), and work_email in profile table row (public.profiles.work_email).';\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- TRIGGERS\n-- ============================================================================\n\n-- Create trigger on auth.users table to link profiles when email changes\n-- Runs AFTER UPDATE to ensure email change is committed\ndrop trigger if exists link_user_to_profile_trigger on auth.users;\n\ncreate trigger link_user_to_profile_trigger\nafter update of email on auth.users\nfor each row\nwhen (old.email is distinct from new.email)\nexecute function public.link_user_to_profile();\n\ncomment on trigger link_user_to_profile_trigger on auth.users is 'Trigger that automatically links profiles to users when auth.users.email changes. Runs after email update to ensure the change is committed before linking.';\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- INITIAL DATA LINKING\n-- ============================================================================\n\n-- Link existing profiles to users based on current email matches\n-- This handles any existing data that needs to be linked\nupdate public.profiles p\nset user_id = u.id\nfrom public.users u\ninner join auth.users au on u.auth_user_id = au.id\nwhere p.work_email = lower(trim(au.email))\n  and (p.user_id is null or p.user_id = u.id);\n\ncomment on table public.profiles is 'User profile data with role and team membership.         "contents": "-- Migration: Link users to profiles based on email matching\n-- Purpose: Automatically links profile rows to user rows when auth.users.email matches profiles.work_email\n-- Affected tables: profiles, users, auth.users\n-- Special considerations: Runs automatically when user email changes in auth.users table\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- FUNCTIONS\n-- ============================================================================\n\n-- Create trigger function to link profiles to users based on email matching\n-- Matches auth.users.email with profiles.work_email and links via public.users\n-- Runs with SECURITY DEFINER to access auth.users table\ncreate or replace function public.link_user_to_profile()\nreturns trigger\nlanguage plpgsql\nsecurity definer\nset search_path = public, auth\nas $$\ndeclare\n  v_user_id uuid;\n  v_auth_email text;\nbegin\n  -- Get the email from auth.users (use NEW.email after update)\n  v_auth_email := new.email;\n  \n  -- Only proceed if email is not null and has changed\n  if v_auth_email is null or v_auth_email = '' then\n    return new;\n  end if;\n  \n  -- Find the public.users row that matches this auth.users.id\n  select id into v_user_id\n  from public.users\n  where auth_user_id = new.id;\n  \n  -- If no matching public.users row found, return early\n  if v_user_id is null then\n    return new;\n  end if;\n  \n  -- Link profile to user if work_email matches auth.users.email\n  -- Only update if profile exists and is not already linked to a different user\n  update public.profiles\n  set user_id = v_user_id\n  where work_email = lower(trim(v_auth_email))\n    and (user_id is null or user_id = v_user_id);\n  \n  return new;\nend;\n$$;\n\ncomment on function public.link_user_to_profile() is 'Trigger function that automatically links profile rows to user rows when auth.users.email matches profiles.work_email. Matches based on currently logged in user email (auth.users.email), uid in user table row (public.users.auth_user_id), and work_email in profile table row (public.profiles.work_email).';\n\n-- ============================================================================",

        "contents": "## Architecture Overview\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart TD\n    subgraph auth_flow [Authentication Flow]\n        A[User clicks Google Login] --&gt; B[Google OAuth]\n        B --&gt; C[Redirect back with Google identity]\n        C --&gt; D{Profile linked to user?}\n        D --&gt;|No| E[Prompt for work email]\n        E --&gt; F{Domain is czu.cz?}\n        F --&gt;|No| G[Show domain error]\n        G --&gt; E\n        F --&gt;|Yes| H[Send OTP to work email]\n        H --&gt; I[User enters OTP]\n        I --&gt; J{Profile exists for work email?}\n        J --&gt;|No| K[Pending Approval Page]\n        J --&gt;|Yes| L[Link profile to user]\n        D --&gt;|Yes| M{Access revoked?}\n        L --&gt; M\n        M --&gt;|Yes| N[Show access revoked]\n        M --&gt;|No| O[Grant Full Access]\n    end\n\n    subgraph request_flow [Request Validation]\n        P[Incoming Request] --&gt; Q[Middleware queries database]\n        Q --&gt; R{Profile linked to user?}\n        R --&gt;|No| S[Redirect to verify email]\n        R --&gt;|Yes| T{removed_access is null?}\n        T --&gt;|No| U[Show access revoked]\n        T --&gt;|Yes| V[Allow access]\n    end\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Validation Flow\n\n**Two-stage validation:**\n\n1. **Before OTP (Domain Check)**: Validate email ends with &#96;@studenti.czu.cz&#96; or &#96;@pef.czu.cz&#96;\n\n   - Client-side: Immediate feedback\n   - Server-side: Validated before &#96;signInWithOtp&#96; is called\n\n2. **After OTP (Profile Linking)**: Check if a profile exists for the verified work email\n\n   - If profile exists with that work_email → link profile to auth.user\n   - If no profile exists → show \"Pending Approval\" (admin must create profile first)\n   - Checked on every request via middleware\n\n## Database Schema (Supabase Migrations)\n\nTwo tables with **no RLS** - all access control is handled in Next.js:\n\n1. **&#96;users&#96;** - Custom table to sync with auth.users (Google OAuth), synced via Next.js server actions\n2. **&#96;profiles&#96;** - User authentication profile data with role and access control\n\n**Important**: No Supabase functions, triggers, or RLS policies. All business logic lives in Next.js.\n\nUse MODDATETIME extension to set the &#96;updated_at&#96; column on every update.",

        "contents": "│ email (google)  │   │   │ name            │\n│ ...auth fields  │   └───│ user_id (1:1)   │\n└─────────────────┘       │ work_email      │\n                          │ role (enum)     │\n                          │ removed_access  │\n                          │ removed_access_by│──┐\n                          │ created_at      │  │\n                          │ updated_at      │  │\n                          └─────────────────┘  │\n                                    ▲          │\n                                    └──────────┘ (self-reference)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Verification Logic\n\n- **Unverified**: &#96;profiles.user_id IS NULL&#96; → User logged in with Google but hasn't verified work email\n- **Pending Approval**: Work email verified via OTP, but no profile exists with that email\n- **Verified &amp; Active**: &#96;profiles.user_id IS NOT NULL AND profiles.removed_access IS NULL&#96;\n- **Access Revoked**: &#96;profiles.removed_access IS NOT NULL&#96;\n\n## Constants\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// lib/constants/auth.ts\nexport const ALLOWED_WORK_EMAIL_DOMAINS = [\n  'studenti.czu.cz',\n  'pef.czu.cz',\n] as const;\n\nexport const isValidWorkEmailDomain = (email: string): boolean =&gt; {\n  const domain = email.split('@')[1]?.toLowerCase();\n  return ALLOWED_WORK_EMAIL_DOMAINS.includes(domain as any);\n};\n\n// Profile roles (matches database enum)\nexport const PROFILE_ROLES = ['student', 'team_leader', 'coach', 'admin'] as const;\nexport type ProfileRole = typeof PROFILE_ROLES[number];\n\n// Role hierarchy for permission checks\nexport const ROLE_HIERARCHY: Record&lt;ProfileRole, number&gt; = {\n  student: 0,\n  team_leader: 1,\n  coach: 2,\n  admin: 3,\n} as const;\n\nexport const hasMinimumRole = (userRole: ProfileRole, requiredRole: ProfileRole): boolean =&gt; {\n  return ROLE_HIERARCHY[userRole] &gt;= ROLE_HIERARCHY[requiredRole];\n};\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Supabase Configuration Changes\n\nUpdate [&#96;supabase/config.toml&#96;](supabase/config.toml):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;toml\n[auth]\nenable_manual_linking = true        # Required for work email linking",

    {
      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./.cursor/plans/work_email_auth_system_467a2b18.plan.md",
        "range": {
          "startPosition": {
            "line": 193
          },
          "endPosition": {

          }
        },
        "contents": "## Supabase Configuration Changes\n\nUpdate [&#96;supabase/config.toml&#96;](supabase/config.toml):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;toml\n[auth]\nenable_manual_linking = true        # Required for work email linking\nenable_anonymous_sign_ins = false   # Block anonymous access\n\n[auth.email]\nenable_signup = false               # Block direct email/password signup\nenable_confirmations = false        # We use OTP for work email, not signup confirmation\n\n[auth.external.google]\nenabled = true\nclient_id = \"env(GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID)\"\nsecret = \"env(GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET)\"\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Profile Verification (Next.js Middleware)\n\nAll verification logic lives in Next.js middleware, not in Supabase:\n\n- **Profile Linked**: Check &#96;profiles.user_id&#96; matches current auth.user.id\n- **Access Active**: Check &#96;profiles.removed_access IS NULL&#96;\n- **User Role**: Read &#96;profiles.role&#96; column (student, team_leader, coach, admin)\n\nThis approach:\n\n- Keeps all business logic in Next.js (single source of truth)\n- Allows real-time updates (e.g., instant access revocation)\n- Admin pre-creates profiles, users link via work email verification\n- Supabase only handles auth + data storage (no custom hooks or functions)\n\n## Development &amp; Testing with Supabase MCP\n\nThe project has a &#96;supabase/&#96; directory with Supabase MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration available for:\n\n1. **Running migrations**: Apply and test database schema changes locally\n2. **Debugging auth flow**: Inspect user sessions and profile data\n3. **Testing verification logic**: Query profiles table for auth checks\n\n**Useful MCP commands for development:**\n\n- Seed test data into profiles table for auth testing\n- Inspect auth.users and profiles tables\n- Test profile linking and access revocation queries\n\n## Key Security Features\n\n### Supabase (Data Layer Only)\n\n1. **Database Constraints**:\n\n   - Domain constraint ensures only valid CZU domains in profiles\n   - Unique constraints on work_email, user_id\n\n2. **No RLS or Functions**:\n\n   - No Row Level Security policies\n   - No database triggers or functions",

        },
        "contents": "await supabase\n  .from('profiles')\n  .update({ \n    user_id: user.id,\n    picture: user.user_metadata.avatar_url  // Default to Google picture\n  })\n  .eq('work_email', workEmail);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Step 4: Middleware Validation\n\nQuery database for profile linked to current auth.user and check &#96;removed_access IS NULL&#96; on every request to protected routes.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// Middleware check\nconst { data: profile } = await supabase\n  .from('profiles')\n  .select('id, role, removed_access')\n  .eq('user_id', user.id)\n  .single();\n\nif (!profile) redirect('/auth/verify-work-email');\nif (profile.removed_access) redirect('/auth/access-revoked');\n// User has active access, continue...\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Estimated Complexity\n\n| Task | Complexity | Lines of Code |\n\n|------|------------|---------------|\n\n| Delete old auth files | Trivial | -500 lines |\n\n| Security lockdown config | Trivial | ~20 lines TOML |\n\n| Database migration | Low | ~40 lines SQL (users, profiles, indexes) |\n\n| Constants + validation | Trivial | ~25 lines |\n\n| Server actions (auth logic) | Medium | ~60 lines |\n\n| Middleware update | Medium | ~50 lines (includes DB queries) |\n\n| Google login page | Low | ~30 lines |\n\n| Work email form + linking | Medium | ~120 lines |\n\n| Pending approval page | Low | ~20 lines |\n\n| Access revoked page | Low | ~20 lines |\n\n**Total new code**: ~385 lines (vs ~500 lines deleted)\n\n## Separation of Concerns\n\n### Supabase (Auth + Storage Only)\n\n- **Authentication**: Google OAuth flow, session management, OTP emails\n- **Database**: Store profiles and users data (no RLS - Next.js handles access control)\n- **No business logic**: No custom hooks, no stored procedures, no triggers, no functions\n\n### Next.js (All Business Logic)\n\n- **Middleware**: Profile verification, access checks, role-based routing\n- **Server Actions**: Profile linking, access revocation\n- **Validation**: Domain validation, input sanitization, business rules\n- **Authorization**: Role hierarchy checks, permission enforcement\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                         Next.js                                  │",

        "contents": "begin\n  v_raw_meta_data := new.raw_user_meta_data;\n  v_google_email := coalesce(new.email, v_raw_meta_data-&gt;&gt;'email');\n  v_google_full_name := v_raw_meta_data-&gt;&gt;'full_name';\n  v_google_profile_picture := coalesce(\n    v_raw_meta_data-&gt;&gt;'avatar_url',\n    v_raw_meta_data-&gt;&gt;'picture'\n  );\n  \n  insert into public.users (\n    auth_user_id,\n    google_email,\n    google_full_name,\n    google_profile_picture\n  )\n  values (\n    new.id,\n    v_google_email,\n    v_google_full_name,\n    v_google_profile_picture\n  );\n  \n  return new;\nend;\n$$;\n\ncomment on function public.handle_new_auth_user() is 'Trigger function that automatically creates a row in public.users table when a new user is created in auth.users. Extracts Google OAuth profile data from auth.users.raw_user_meta_data.';\n\n-- Create validation trigger function for CZU email domain\n-- Ensures that email addresses being changed must end with @pef.czu.cz or @studenti.czu.cz\ncreate or replace function public.validate_czu_email_domain_trigger()\nreturns trigger\nlanguage plpgsql\nsecurity definer\nset search_path = public, auth\nas $$\ndeclare\n  v_email text;\n  v_email_change text;\n  v_domain text;\nbegin\n  if tg_op != 'UPDATE' then\n    return NEW;\n  end if;",

    {
      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./supabase/migrations/20260131000000_initial_schema.sql",

        "contents": "begin\n  v_encrypted_password := event-&gt;'user'-&gt;&gt;'encrypted_password';\n  \n  if v_encrypted_password is not null then\n    raise exception 'Password-based signups are not allowed. Please use Google OAuth to sign in.';\n  end if;\n  \n  v_provider := event-&gt;'user'-&gt;'raw_user_meta_data'-&gt;&gt;'provider';\n  v_app_metadata := event-&gt;'user'-&gt;'app_metadata';\n  if v_provider is null and v_app_metadata is not null then\n    v_provider := v_app_metadata-&gt;&gt;'provider';\n  end if;\n  \n  if event-&gt;'user'-&gt;'identities' is not null then\n    for v_identity in \n      select value from jsonb_array_elements(event-&gt;'user'-&gt;'identities')\n    loop\n      if v_identity-&gt;&gt;'provider' = 'google' then\n        v_has_google_identity := true;\n        exit;\n      end if;\n    end loop;\n  end if;\n  \n  if v_provider = 'google' or v_has_google_identity then\n    return event;\n  end if;\n  \n  raise exception 'Only Google OAuth signups are allowed. Please use Google to sign in.';\nend;\n$$;\n\ncomment on function public.before_user_created_hook(jsonb) is 'Hook function that restricts signups to Google OAuth only. Blocks password-based and OTP signups.';\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- TRIGGERS\n-- ============================================================================\n\n-- Create triggers for updated_at on all tables\ncreate trigger users_updated_at_trigger\nbefore update on public.users\nfor each row\nexecute function public.handle_updated_at();\n\ncreate trigger teams_updated_at_trigger\nbefore update on public.teams\nfor each row\nexecute function public.handle_updated_at();\n\ncreate trigger profiles_updated_at_trigger\nbefore update on public.profiles\nfor each row\nexecute function public.handle_updated_at();\n\n-- Create trigger on auth.users table to populate public.users\ndrop trigger if exists on_auth_user_created on auth.users;\n\ncreate trigger on_auth_user_created\nafter insert on auth.users\nfor each row\nexecute function public.handle_new_auth_user();\n\n-- Create trigger on auth.users table for email domain validation\ndrop trigger if exists validate_czu_email_domain_trigger on auth.users;",

        "contents": "   - No Row Level Security policies\n   - No database triggers or functions\n   - All access control handled by Next.js\n\n### Next.js (Application Layer - All Business Logic)\n\n1. **Middleware Verification**:\n\n   - Queries &#96;profiles&#96; table for linked user_id\n   - Checks &#96;removed_access&#96; is null for active access\n   - Enforces role-based route protection\n   - Real-time verification (instant access revocation)\n\n2. **Domain Validation** (in server actions):\n\n   - Client-side validation for UX (immediate feedback)\n   - Server-side validation before sending OTP\n   - Validates email format and CZU domain\n\n3. **Access Management** (in server actions):\n\n   - Admin sets &#96;removed_access&#96; timestamp and &#96;removed_access_by&#96; profile\n   - Immediate effect on next request\n   - Audit trail of who revoked access and when\n\n## Authentication Flow Details\n\n### Step 1: Google Login\n\nUser clicks Google login button, Supabase handles OAuth flow.\n\n### Step 2: Work Email Input with Domain Validation\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// Validate domain before sending OTP\nif (!isValidWorkEmailDomain(workEmail)) {\n  throw new Error('Email must be @studenti.czu.cz or @pef.czu.cz');\n}\n\n// Send OTP to work email (only after domain validation passes)\nconst { error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithOtp({\n  email: workEmail,\n  options: { shouldCreateUser: false }\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Step 3: OTP Verification and Profile Linking\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// After user enters OTP, verify it\nconst { error } = await supabase.auth.verifyOtp({\n  email: workEmail,\n  token: otpCode,\n  type: 'email'\n});\n\n// Check if profile exists for this work email\nconst { data: profile } = await supabase\n  .from('profiles')\n  .select('id')\n  .eq('work_email', workEmail)\n  .single();\n\nif (!profile) {\n  // No profile exists - redirect to pending approval\n  redirect('/auth/pending-approval');\n}\n\n// Link profile to current user\nconst { data: { user } } = await supabase.auth.getUser();\nawait supabase\n  .from('profiles')\n  .update({ \n    user_id: user.id,",

        "contents": "└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n                           │\n                           ▼\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                        Supabase                                  │\n│  ┌─────────────────────┐  ┌─────────────────────────────────┐   │\n│  │   Auth Service      │  │         PostgreSQL              │   │\n│  │  - Google OAuth     │  │  - profiles table               │   │\n│  │  - OTP emails       │  │  - users table                  │   │\n│  │  - Session mgmt     │  │  - No RLS (Next.js handles)     │   │\n│  └─────────────────────┘  └─────────────────────────────────┘   │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n\n## Simplicity Principles\n\n1. **Business logic in Next.js** - Server actions and middleware handle all rules\n2. **Supabase for storage only** - No hooks, no custom functions, no RLS, just tables\n3. **Minimal components** - Reuse shadcn/ui, no custom abstractions\n4. **Direct database queries** - Query profiles table for verification and access status\n5. **Admin-first onboarding** - Admin creates profiles, users link via work email verification\n\n# Common Traps to Avoid\n\n1. The auth flow will get stuck once the user is redirected back to the nextjs app from supabase.",

            "text": "3. **Minimal components** - Reuse shadcn/ui, no custom abstractions",

        "contents": "Got it — here’s your **agent-optimized PRD template in Markdown (&#96;.md&#96;)** so you can reuse it for any product:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;&#96;markdown\n# PRD — [Product Name] MVP\n\n## 1. Overview\n[One-paragraph description of the product. Include key functionality, user interactions, and constraints like onboarding or payment.]\n\n---\n\n## 2. System Goals\n- [Goal 1: core outcome]\n- [Goal 2: workflows to automate or improve]\n- [Goal 3: monetization / business value]\n\n---\n\n## 3. Entities &amp; Schemas\n\n### Example: &#96;users&#96;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate table users (\n  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),\n  email text unique not null,\n  phone text unique,\n  created_at timestamptz default now()\n);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Example: &#96;subscriptions&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate table subscriptions (\n  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),\n  user_id uuid references users(id),\n  stripe_customer_id text,\n  stripe_subscription_id text,\n  status text check (status in ('active','canceled','past_due')),\n  created_at timestamptz default now()\n);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n\\[Add more entities as needed: &#96;messages&#96;, &#96;tasks&#96;, &#96;reminders&#96;, etc.]\n\n---\n\n## 4. Features\n\n### 4.1 Onboarding &amp; Payment\n\n* **Signup:** \\[Auth provider]\n* **Phone Verification:**\n\n  * Input: &#96;{ phone_number }&#96;\n  * Output: &#96;{ success: true, otp_sent: true }&#96;\n* **Payment:** Stripe/PayPal/etc → subscription sync\n\n### 4.2 Channels / Interfaces\n\n#### Web Chat\n\n* Input: &#96;{ user_id, message }&#96;\n* Output: &#96;{ status: \"stored\", assistant_reply }&#96;\n* Flow:\n\n  1. Store in DB\n  2. Call LLM agent with context\n  3.         "contents": "comment on function public.handle_user_update_restriction() is 'Trigger function that restricts user updates to suggested_work_email only. Automatically updates last_otp_sent_at when suggested_work_email changes. Prevents modification of all other fields including google_email, google_profile_picture, google_full_name, auth_user_id, id, and created_at.';\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- TRIGGERS\n-- ============================================================================\n\n-- Create trigger to enforce update restrictions on users table\n-- This trigger runs BEFORE the update to prevent field modifications\ndrop trigger if exists users_update_restriction_trigger on public.users;\n\ncreate trigger users_update_restriction_trigger\nbefore update on public.users\nfor each row\nexecute function public.handle_user_update_restriction();\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- RLS POLICIES\n-- ============================================================================\n\n-- Drop the existing permissive update policy\ndrop policy if exists \"Users can update their own user record\" on public.users;\n\n-- Create a new restrictive update policy that only allows updating suggested_work_email\n-- The trigger function will enforce that only suggested_work_email can be changed\ncreate policy \"Users can update only suggested_work_email\" on public.users\nfor update\nto authenticated\nusing ( (select auth.uid()) = auth_user_id )\nwith check ( (select auth.uid()) = auth_user_id );\n\ncomment on policy \"Users can update only suggested_work_email\" on public.users is 'RLS policy that allows authenticated users to update only their own user record. The handle_user_update_restriction() trigger enforces that only suggested_work_email can be modified, and automatically updates last_otp_sent_at.';\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- GRANTS\n-- ============================================================================\n\n-- Grant execute permissions for the new trigger function",
        "signatures": {},

        "contents": "-- Migration: Restrict user updates to suggested_work_email only\n-- Purpose: Allows users to only update suggested_work_email field, automatically updates last_otp_sent_at\n-- Affected tables: users\n-- Special considerations: Prevents users from modifying any other fields in the users table\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- FUNCTIONS\n-- ============================================================================\n\n-- Create trigger function to restrict updates to suggested_work_email only\n-- Automatically updates last_otp_sent_at when suggested_work_email changes\n-- Prevents users from modifying any other fields in the users table\ncreate or replace function public.handle_user_update_restriction()\nreturns trigger\nlanguage plpgsql\nsecurity definer\nset search_path = public, auth\nas $$\nbegin\n  -- Allow only suggested_work_email to be changed\n  -- Reset all other fields to their original values to prevent modification\n  new.id := old.id;\n  new.auth_user_id := old.auth_user_id;\n  new.google_email := old.google_email;\n  new.google_profile_picture := old.google_profile_picture;\n  new.google_full_name := old.google_full_name;\n  new.created_at := old.created_at;\n  \n  -- Automatically update last_otp_sent_at when suggested_work_email changes\n  if old.suggested_work_email is distinct from new.suggested_work_email then\n    new.last_otp_sent_at := now();\n  else\n    -- Keep existing last_otp_sent_at if suggested_work_email hasn't changed\n    new.last_otp_sent_at := old.last_otp_sent_at;\n  end if;\n  \n  -- updated_at is handled by the existing handle_updated_at() trigger\n  -- so we don't need to set it here\n  \n  return new;\nend;\n$$;\n\ncomment on function public.handle_user_update_restriction() is 'Trigger function that restricts user updates to suggested_work_email only. Automatically updates last_otp_sent_at when suggested_work_email changes. Prevents modification of all other fields including google_email, google_profile_picture, google_full_name, auth_user_id, id, and created_at.';\n\n-- ============================================================================",

        "contents": "### &#96;auth.jwt()&#96;\n\nReturns the JWT of the user making the request. Anything that you store in the user's &#96;raw_app_meta_data&#96; column or the &#96;raw_user_meta_data&#96; column will be accessible using this function. It's important to know the distinction between these two:\n\n- &#96;raw_user_meta_data&#96; - can be updated by the authenticated user using the &#96;supabase.auth.update()&#96; function. It is not a good place to store authorization data.\n- &#96;raw_app_meta_data&#96; - cannot be updated by the user, so it's a good place to store authorization data.\n\nThe &#96;auth.jwt()&#96; function is extremely versatile. For example, if you store some team data inside &#96;app_metadata&#96;, you can use it to determine whether a particular user belongs to a team. For example, if this was an array of IDs:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"User is in team\"\non my_table\nto authenticated\nusing ( team_id in (select auth.jwt() -&gt; 'app_metadata' -&gt; 'teams'));\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### MFA\n\nThe &#96;auth.jwt()&#96; function can be used to check for [Multi-Factor Authentication](mdc:docs/guides/auth/auth-mfa#enforce-rules-for-mfa-logins). For example, you could restrict a user from updating their profile unless they have at least 2 levels of authentication (Assurance Level 2):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Restrict updates.\"\non profiles\nas restrictive\nfor update\nto authenticated using (\n  (select auth.jwt()-&gt;&gt;'aal') = 'aal2'\n);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## RLS performance recommendations\n\nEvery authorization system has an impact on performance. While row level security is powerful, the performance impact is important to keep in mind. This is especially true for queries that scan every row in a table - like many &#96;select&#96; operations, including those using limit, offset, and ordering.\n\nBased on a series of [tests](mdc:https:/github.com/GaryAustin1/RLS-Performance), we have a few recommendations for RLS:\n\n### Add indexes\n\nMake sure you've added [indexes](mdc:docs/guides/database/postgres/indexes) on any columns used within the Policies which are not already indexed (or primary keys). For a Policy like this:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Users can access their own records\" on test_table",

Provided domain: %', v_domain;\n      end if;\n    end if;\n  end if;\n\n  if OLD.email is distinct from NEW.email then\n    v_email := NEW.email;\n    \n    if v_email is not null and v_email != '' then\n      v_domain := lower(split_part(v_email, '@', 2));\n      \n      if v_domain not in ('pef.czu.cz', 'studenti.czu.cz') then\n        raise exception 'Email must end with @pef.czu.cz or @studenti.czu.cz. Provided domain: %', v_domain;\n      end if;\n    end if;\n  end if;\n\n  return NEW;\nend;\n$$;\n\ncomment on function public.validate_czu_email_domain_trigger() is 'Server-side trigger function that validates email domains at the database level.         "contents": "- &#96;anon&#96;: an unauthenticated request (the user is not logged in)\n- &#96;authenticated&#96;: an authenticated request (the user is logged in)\n\nThese are actually [Postgres Roles](mdc:docs/guides/database/postgres/roles). You can use these roles within your Policies using the &#96;TO&#96; clause:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Profiles are viewable by everyone\"\non profiles\nfor select\nto authenticated, anon\nusing ( true );\n\n-- OR\n\ncreate policy \"Public profiles are viewable only by authenticated users\"\non profiles\nfor select\nto authenticated\nusing ( true );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nNote that &#96;for ...&#96; must be added after the table but before the roles. &#96;to ...&#96; must be added after &#96;for ...&#96;:\n\n### Incorrect\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Public profiles are viewable only by authenticated users\"\non profiles\nto authenticated\nfor select\nusing ( true );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Correct\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Public profiles are viewable only by authenticated users\"\non profiles\nfor select\nto authenticated\nusing ( true );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Multiple operations\n\nPostgreSQL policies do not support specifying multiple operations in a single FOR clause. You need to create separate policies for each operation.\n\n### Incorrect\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Profiles can be created and deleted by any user\"\non profiles\nfor insert, delete -- cannot create a policy on multiple operators\nto authenticated\nwith check ( true )\nusing ( true );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Correct\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Profiles can be created by any user\"\non profiles\nfor insert\nto authenticated\nwith check ( true );\n\ncreate policy \"Profiles can be deleted by any user\"\non profiles\nfor delete\nto authenticated\nusing ( true );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Helper functions\n\nSupabase provides some helper functions that make it easier to write Policies.\n\n### &#96;auth.uid()&#96;\n\nReturns the ID of the user making the request.\n\n### &#96;auth.jwt()&#96;\n\nReturns the JWT of the user making the request. Anything that you store in the user's &#96;raw_app_meta_data&#96; column or the &#96;raw_user_meta_data&#96; column will be accessible using this function. It's important to know the distinction between these two:\n\n- &#96;raw_user_meta_data&#96; - can be updated by the authenticated user using the &#96;supabase.auth.update()&#96; function. It is not a good place to store authorization data.",

        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "- &#96;anon&#96;: an unauthenticated request (the user is not logged in)",

          },
          {
            "text": "- &#96;authenticated&#96;: an authenticated request (the user is logged in)",
            "lineNumber": 42
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 43
          },
          {
            "text": "These are actually [Postgres Roles](mdc:docs/guides/database/postgres/roles). You can use these roles within your Policies using the &#96;TO&#96; clause:",

          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 45
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;sql",
            "lineNumber": 46
          },
          {
            "text": "create policy \"Profiles are viewable by everyone\"",
            "lineNumber": 47
          },
          {
            "text": "on profiles",
            "lineNumber": 48
          },
          {
            "text": "for select",
            "lineNumber": 49

        "contents": "## Architecture Overview\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart TD\n    subgraph auth_flow [Authentication Flow]\n        A[User clicks Google Login] --&gt; B[Google OAuth]\n        B --&gt; C[Redirect back with Google identity]\n        C --&gt; D{Profile linked to user?}\n        D --&gt;|No| E[Prompt for work email]\n        E --&gt; F{Domain is czu.cz?}\n        F --&gt;|No| G[Show domain error]\n        G --&gt; E\n        F --&gt;|Yes| H[Send OTP to work email]\n        H --&gt; I[User enters OTP]\n        I --&gt; J{Profile exists for work email?}\n        J --&gt;|No| K[Pending Approval Page]\n        J --&gt;|Yes| L[Link profile to user]\n        D --&gt;|Yes| M{Access revoked?}\n        L --&gt; M\n        M --&gt;|Yes| N[Show access revoked]\n        M --&gt;|No| O[Grant Full Access]\n    end\n\n    subgraph request_flow [Request Validation]\n        P[Incoming Request] --&gt; Q[Middleware queries database]\n        Q --&gt; R{Profile linked to user?}\n        R --&gt;|No| S[Redirect to verify email]\n        R --&gt;|Yes| T{removed_access is null?}\n        T --&gt;|No| U[Show access revoked]\n        T --&gt;|Yes| V[Allow access]\n    end\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Validation Flow\n\n**Two-stage validation:**\n\n1. **Before OTP (Domain Check)**: Validate email ends with &#96;@studenti.czu.cz&#96;         "contents": "export async function updateSession(request: NextRequest) {\n\n    !user &amp;&amp;\n    !request.nextUrl.pathname.startsWith(\"/login\") &amp;&amp;\n    !request.nextUrl.pathname.startsWith(\"/auth\")\n  ) {\n    // no user, potentially respond by redirecting the user to the login page\n    const url = request.nextUrl.clone();\n    url.pathname = \"/auth/login\";\n    return NextResponse.redirect(url);\n  }\n\n  // IMPORTANT: You *must* return the supabaseResponse object as it is.\n  // If you're creating a new response object with NextResponse.next() make sure to:\n  // 1.         "contents": "   - No Row Level Security policies\n   - No database triggers or functions\n   - All access control handled by Next.js\n\n### Next.js (Application Layer - All Business Logic)\n\n1. **Middleware Verification**:\n\n   - Queries &#96;profiles&#96; table for linked user_id\n   - Checks &#96;removed_access&#96; is null for active access\n   - Enforces role-based route protection\n   - Real-time verification (instant access revocation)\n\n2. **Domain Validation** (in server actions):\n\n   - Client-side validation for UX (immediate feedback)\n   - Server-side validation before sending OTP\n   - Validates email format and CZU domain\n\n3. **Access Management** (in server actions):\n\n   - Admin sets &#96;removed_access&#96; timestamp and &#96;removed_access_by&#96; profile\n   - Immediate effect on next request\n   - Audit trail of who revoked access and when\n\n## Authentication Flow Details\n\n### Step 1: Google Login\n\nUser clicks Google login button, Supabase handles OAuth flow.\n\n### Step 2: Work Email Input with Domain Validation\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// Validate domain before sending OTP\nif (!isValidWorkEmailDomain(workEmail)) {\n  throw new Error('Email must be @studenti.czu.cz or @pef.czu.cz');\n}\n\n// Send OTP to work email (only after domain validation passes)\nconst { error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithOtp({\n  email: workEmail,\n  options: { shouldCreateUser: false }\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Step 3: OTP Verification and Profile Linking\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// After user enters OTP, verify it\nconst { error } = await supabase.auth.verifyOtp({\n  email: workEmail,\n  token: otpCode,\n  type: 'email'\n});\n\n// Check if profile exists for this work email\nconst { data: profile } = await supabase\n  .from('profiles')\n  .select('id')\n  .eq('work_email', workEmail)\n  .single();\n\nif (!profile) {\n  // No profile exists - redirect to pending approval\n  redirect('/auth/pending-approval');\n}\n\n// Link profile to current user\nconst { data: { user } } = await supabase.auth.getUser();\nawait supabase\n  .from('profiles')\n  .update({ \n    user_id: user.id,",
