        "contents": "export function VerifyEmailForm() {\n;\n\n  return (\n    &lt;Card&gt;\n      &lt;CardHeader&gt;\n        &lt;CardTitle className=\"text-2xl\"&gt;Verify Email&lt;/CardTitle&gt;\n        &lt;CardDescription&gt;\n          {step === \"email\"\n            ? \"Link an email address to your account using OTP verification\"\n            : &#96;Enter the OTP code sent to ${email || \"your email\"}&#96;}\n        &lt;/CardDescription&gt;\n      &lt;/CardHeader&gt;\n      &lt;CardContent&gt;\n        {error &amp;&amp; (\n          &lt;div className=\"mb-4 p-3 text-sm text-destructive bg-destructive/10 rounded-md\"&gt;\n            {error}\n          &lt;/div&gt;\n        )}\n\n        {step === \"email\" ? (\n          &lt;form onSubmit={handleSendOTP} className=\"flex flex-col gap-4\"&gt;\n            &lt;div className=\"flex flex-col gap-2\"&gt;\n              &lt;Label htmlFor=\"email\"&gt;Email Address&lt;/Label&gt;\n              &lt;Input\n                id=\"email\"\n                type=\"email\"\n                placeholder=\"your.email@pef.czu.cz\"\n                value={email}\n                onChange={(e) =&gt; setEmail(e.target.value)}\n                disabled={isLoading}\n                required\n                autoFocus\n              /&gt;\n              &lt;p className=\"text-xs text-muted-foreground\"&gt;\n                Email must end with @pef.czu.cz or @studenti.czu.cz\n              &lt;/p&gt;\n            &lt;/div&gt;\n            &lt;Button type=\"submit\" disabled={isLoading} className=\"w-full\"&gt;\n              {isLoading ? \"Sending...\" : \"Send OTP Code\"}\n            &lt;/Button&gt;\n          &lt;/form&gt;\n        ) : (\n          &lt;form onSubmit={handleVerifyOTP} className=\"flex flex-col gap-4\"&gt;\n            &lt;div className=\"flex flex-col gap-2\"&gt;\n}",

        "contents": "export function VerifyEmailForm() {\nconst handleSendOTP = async  {\n    e.preventDefault();\n    setError(null);\n    setIsLoading(true);\n\n    try {\n      // Validate email format\n      if (!email || !email.includes(\"@\")) {\n        setError(\"Please enter a valid email address\");\n        setIsLoading(false);\n        return;\n      }\n\n      // Validate CZU domain\n      if (!isValidWorkEmailDomain(email.trim())) {\n        setError(\"Email must end with @pef.czu.cz or @studenti.czu.cz\");\n        setIsLoading(false);\n        return;\n      }\n\n      // Use updateUser to add email identity to existing authenticated user\n      // This sends a verification link to the email address\n      // With enable_manual_linking = true, this will link the email identity\n      // Note: This adds the email as a secondary identity, not changing the primary email\n      const { data: updateData, error: updateError } = await supabase.auth.updateUser(\n        {\n          email: email.trim(),\n        },\n      );\n\n      if (updateError) {\n        // If email already exists, that's actually fine - it means it might already be linked\n        // or we need to handle it differently\n        if (updateError.message?.includes(\"already registered\")) {\n          setError(\"This email is already registered. Please use a different email or sign in with that email.\");\n        } else {\n          setError(updateError.message || \"Failed to send OTP code\");\n        }\n        setIsLoading(false);\n        return;\n      }\n\n      // Move to OTP verification step\n      setStep(\"otp\");\n      savePersistedState({ step: \"otp\", email: email.trim() });\n      setIsLoading(false);\n    } catch (err) {\n      setError(\"An unexpected error occurred\");\n      setIsLoading(false);\n    }\n  };\n\n  /**\n   * Verifies the OTP code and links email identity to user\n   * Uses type 'email_change' since we're updating the user's email via updateUser()\n   * With enable_manual_linking = true, this will link the email identity\n   * to the existing authenticated user account\n   */\n}",

        "contents": "import { createClient } from \"@/lib/supabase/server\";\nimport { InfoIcon } from \"lucide-react\";\nimport { FetchDataSteps } from \"@/components/tutorial/fetch-data-steps\";\nimport { Suspense } from \"react\";\n\nasync function UserDetails() {\n  const supabase = await createClient();\n  const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.getClaims();\n\n  if (error || !data?.claims) {\n    redirect(\"/auth/login\");\n  }\n\n  return JSON.stringify(data.claims, null, 2);\n}\n\nexport default function ProtectedPage() {\n  return\n}",

        "contents": "---\nname: Work Email Auth System\noverview: Build a robust authentication system using Supabase with Google OAuth, work email verification (@studenti.czu.cz or @pef.czu.cz)\ntodos:\n  - id: db-schema\n    content: Create Supabase migration for users and profiles tables (no RLS - access control in Next.js)\n    status: pending\n  - id: profile-verification\n    content: Implement database-based profile verification (no JWT claims)\n    status: pending\n  - id: supabase-config\n    content: Update supabase/config.toml (manual_linking, Google OAuth, security settings)\n    status: pending\n  - id: auth-constants\n    content: Create lib/constants/auth.ts with domain validation and role constants\n    status: pending\n  - id: server-actions\n    content: Create lib/actions/auth.ts with profile linking, verification, and access revocation\n    status: pending\n  - id: middleware-update\n    content: Update proxy.ts to query profiles table for verified user and access status\n    status: pending\n  - id: google-login\n    content: Create Google login button and rewrite login page\n    status: pending\n  - id: verify-email-flow\n    content: Create work email verification page with OTP and identity linking\n    status: pending\n  - id: pending-approval-page\n    content: Create pending approval page for users without profiles\n    status: pending\n  - id: access-revoked-page\n    content: Create access revoked page for users with revoked access\n    status: pending\n---\n\n# Work Email Authentication System\n\n## Architecture Overview\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart TD\n    subgraph auth_flow [Authentication Flow]\n        ",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "---",
            "lineNumber": 1
          },
          {
            "text": "name: Work Email Auth System",
            "lineNumber": 2

          {
            "text": "overview: Build a robust authentication system using Supabase with Google OAuth, work email verification (@studenti.czu.cz or @pef.czu.cz)",
            "lineNumber": 3
          },
          {
            "text": "todos:",
            "lineNumber": 4

          {
            "text": "  - id: db-schema",

          {
            "text": "    content: Create Supabase migration for users and profiles tables (no RLS - access control in Next.js)",

        "contents": "export function VerifyEmailForm() {\nconst handleSendOTP = async \n\n    }\n  };\n\n  /**\n   * Verifies the OTP code and links email identity to user\n   * Uses type 'email_change' since we're updating the user's email via updateUser()\n   * With enable_manual_linking = true, this will link the email identity\n   * to the existing authenticated user account\n   */\n  const verifyOTP = useCallback(async () =&gt; {\n    setError(null);\n    setIsLoading(true);\n\n    try {\n      // Verify OTP code for email change/linking\n      // Use type 'email_change' because we used updateUser() to initiate the flow\n      // With enable_manual_linking = true, this will link the email identity\n      // to the current authenticated user instead of creating a new user\n      const { error: verifyError } = await supabase.auth.verifyOtp({\n        email: email.trim(),\n        token: otpCode.trim(),\n        type: \"email_change\",\n      });\n\n      if (verifyError) {\n        setError(verifyError.message || \"Invalid OTP code\");\n        setIsLoading(false);\n        return;\n      }\n\n      // Refresh session to ensure identities are updated\n      await supabase.auth.refreshSession();\n\n      // Clear persisted state on success\n      clearPersistedState();\n\n      // Success - redirect to protected page\n      router.push(\"/protected\");\n      router.refresh();\n    } catch (err) {\n      setError(\"An unexpected error occurred\");\n      setIsLoading(false);\n    }\n  }, [email, otpCode, supabase, router]);\n\n  /**\n   * Handles form submission for OTP verification\n   */\n  const handleVerifyOTP = async (e: React.FormEvent) =&gt; {\n    e.preventDefault();\n    await verifyOTP();\n  };\n\n  /**\n   * Loads persisted state from sessionStorage after component mounts (client-side only)\n   * This prevents hydration mismatches between server and client\n   */\n}",

        "contents": "export async function updateSession(request: NextRequest) {\n\n\n  // Redirect to login if not authenticated (except for public routes)\n  if (!isPublicRoute &amp;&amp; !user) {\n    const url = request.nextUrl.clone();\n    url.pathname = \"/auth/login\";\n    return NextResponse.redirect(url);\n  }\n\n  // Check for linked profile if user is authenticated and not on public routes\n  if (user &amp;&amp; !isPublicRoute) {\n    // Get the public.users row linked to this auth user\n    const { data: publicUser } = await supabase\n      .from(\"users\")\n      .select(\"id\")\n      .eq(\"auth_user_id\", user.sub)\n      .single();\n\n    if (publicUser) {\n      // Check if there's a profile linked to this user\n      const { data: profile } = await supabase\n        .from(\"profiles\")\n        .select(\"id\")\n        .eq(\"user_id\", publicUser.id)\n        .single();\n\n      if (!profile) {\n        // User doesn't have a linked profile, redirect to pending approval\n        const url = request.nextUrl.clone();\n        url.pathname = \"/auth/pending-approval\";\n        return NextResponse.redirect(url);\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  // IMPORTANT: You *must* return the supabaseResponse object as it is.\n  // If you're creating a new response object with NextResponse.next() make sure to:\n  // 1. Pass the request in it, like so:\n  //    const myNewResponse = NextResponse.next({ request })\n  // 2. Copy over the cookies, like so:\n  //    myNewResponse.cookies.setAll(supabaseResponse.cookies.getAll())\n  // 3. Change the myNewResponse object to fit your needs, but avoid changing\n  //    the cookies!\n  // 4. Finally:\n  //    return myNewResponse\n  // If this is not done, you may be causing the browser and server to go out\n  // of sync and terminate the user's session prematurely!\n\n  return supabaseResponse;\n}",

        "contents": "/**\n * Checks if the authenticated user has a linked profile\n * @returns true if user has a linked profile, false otherwise\n */\nexport async function hasLinkedProfile(): Promise&lt;boolean&gt; {\n  const supabase = await createClient();\n  const { data: { user }, error } = await supabase.auth.getUser();\n\n  if (error || !user) {\n    return false;\n  }\n\n  // Get the public.users row linked to this auth user\n  const { data: publicUser } = await supabase\n    .from(\"users\")\n    .select(\"id\")\n    .eq(\"auth_user_id\", user.id)\n    .single();\n\n  if (!publicUser) {\n    return false;\n  }\n\n  // Check if there's a profile linked to this user\n  const { data: profile } = await supabase\n    .from(\"profiles\")\n    .select(\"id\")\n    .eq(\"user_id\", publicUser.id)\n    .single();\n\n  return !!profile;\n}",

        "contents": "import { NextResponse, type NextRequest } from \"next/server\";\n\nexport async function updateSession(request: NextRequest) {\n  let supabaseResponse = NextResponse.next({\n    request,\n  });\n\n  // If the env vars are not set, skip proxy check. You can remove this\n  // once you setup the project.\n\n  // With Fluid compute, don't put this client in a global environment\n  // variable. Always create a new one on each request.\n  const supabase = createServerClient(\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL!,\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY!,\n    {\n      cookies: {\n        getAll() {\n          return request.cookies.getAll();\n        },\n        setAll(cookiesToSet) {\n          cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value }) =&gt;\n            request.cookies.set(name, value),\n          );\n          supabaseResponse = NextResponse.next({\n            request,\n          });\n          cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value, options }) =&gt;\n            supabaseResponse.cookies.set(name, value, options),\n          );\n        },\n      },\n    },\n  );\n\n  // Do not run code between createServerClient and\n  // supabase.auth.getClaims(). A simple mistake could make it very hard to debug\n  // issues with users being randomly logged out.\n\n  // IMPORTANT: If you remove getClaims() and you use server-side rendering\n  // with the Supabase client, your users may be randomly logged out.\n  const { data } = await supabase.auth.getClaims();\n  const user = data?.claims;\n\n  const pathname = request.nextUrl.pathname;\n  const isPublicRoute = pathname === \"/\" || pathname.startsWith(\"/auth\");\n\n  // Redirect to login if not authenticated (except for public routes)\n}",

    {
      "codeBlock": {

          }
        },
        "contents": "/**\n * Checks if the authenticated user has an email identity linked\n * (not just OAuth providers like Google)\n * @returns true if user has an email identity, false otherwise\n */\nexport async function hasEmailIdentity(): Promise&lt;boolean&gt; {\n  const supabase = await createClient();\n  const { data: { user }, error } = await supabase.auth.getUser();\n\n  if (error || !user) {\n    return false;\n  }\n\n  // Check if user has an email identity (not just OAuth)\n  // User identities include: email, google, etc.\n  // We need at least one email identity\n  const identities = user.identities || [];\n\n  // Check if any identity is an email identity (not OAuth)\n  return identities.some(\n    (identity) =&gt; identity.provider === \"email\"\n  );\n}\n\n/**\n * Checks if the authenticated user has a linked profile\n * @returns true if user has a linked profile, false otherwise\n */",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "/**",
            "lineNumber": 3
          },
          {
            "text": " * Checks if the authenticated user has an email identity linked",
            "lineNumber": 4
          },
          {
            "text": " * (not just OAuth providers like Google)",
            "lineNumber": 5
          },
          {
            "text": " * @returns true if user has an email identity, false otherwise",
            "lineNumber": 6
          },
          {
            "text": " */",
            "lineNumber": 7

        "contents": "&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Users can access their own records\" on test_table\nto authenticated\nusing ( (select auth.uid()) = user_id );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nYou can add an index like:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate index userid\non test_table\nusing btree (user_id);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Call functions with &#96;select&#96;\n\nYou can use &#96;select&#96; statement to improve policies that use functions. For example, instead of this:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Users can access their own records\" on test_table\nto authenticated\nusing ( auth.uid() = user_id );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nYou can do:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Users can access their own records\" on test_table\nto authenticated\nusing ( (select auth.uid()) = user_id );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis method works well for JWT functions like &#96;auth.uid()&#96; and &#96;auth.jwt()&#96; as well as &#96;security definer&#96; Functions.         "contents": "for select\nto authenticated\nusing ( (select auth.uid()) = auth_user_id );\n\n-- Users can update their own user record\ncreate policy \"Users can update their own user record\" on public.users\nfor update\nto authenticated\nusing ( (select auth.uid()) = auth_user_id )\nwith check ( (select auth.uid()) = auth_user_id );\n\n-- Users can insert their own user record (during signup via trigger)\ncreate policy \"Users can insert their own user record\" on public.users\nfor insert\nto authenticated\nwith check ( (select auth.uid()) = auth_user_id );\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- RLS POLICIES - PROFILES TABLE\n-- ============================================================================\n\n-- Users can view their own profile\ncreate policy \"Users can view their own profile\" on public.profiles\nfor select\nto authenticated\nusing (\n  user_id in (\n    select id\n    from public.users\n    where auth_user_id = (select auth.uid())\n  )\n);\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- RLS POLICIES - REALTIME MESSAGES TABLE\n-- ============================================================================\n\n-- Users can receive broadcasts for their own user record\ncreate policy \"Users can receive broadcasts for their own user record\" on realtime.messages\nfor select\nto authenticated\nusing (\n  topic like 'users:%'\n  and exists (\n    select 1\n    from public.users\n    where auth_user_id = (select auth.uid())\n    and topic = 'users:' || id::text\n  )\n);\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- GRANTS\n-- ============================================================================\n\n-- Grant execute permissions for trigger functions\ngrant execute on function public.handle_new_auth_user() to authenticated;\ngrant execute on function public.handle_new_auth_user() to anon;\ngrant execute on function public.validate_czu_email_domain_trigger() to authenticated;\ngrant execute on function public.validate_czu_email_domain_trigger() to anon;\ngrant execute on function public.before_user_created_hook(jsonb) to authenticated;",

        "contents": "import { redirect } from \"next/navigation\";\nimport { type NextRequest } from \"next/server\";\n\nimport { hasEmailIdentity } from \"@/lib/auth-helpers\";\n\n/**\n * Handles OAuth callback from Google\n * Exchanges the code for a session and redirects appropriately\n */\nexport async function GET(request: NextRequest) {\n  const { searchParams, origin } = new URL(request.url);\n  const code = searchParams.get(\"code\");\n  const next = searchParams.get(\"next\");\n\n  if (code) {\n    const supabase = await createClient();\n    const { error } = await supabase.auth.exchangeCodeForSession(code);\n\n    if (!error) {\n      // Check if user has email identity linked\n      // If not, redirect to verify-email page\n      const hasEmail = await hasEmailIdentity();\n      const redirectTo = next || (hasEmail ? \"/protected\" : \"/auth/verify-email\");\n      redirect(redirectTo);\n    }\n  }\n\n  // Redirect to error page if something went wrong\n  redirect(&#96;/auth/error?error=Failed to authenticate with Google&#96;);\n}",

        "contents": "### &#96;auth.jwt()&#96;\n\nReturns the JWT of the user making the request. Anything that you store in the user's &#96;raw_app_meta_data&#96; column or the &#96;raw_user_meta_data&#96; column will be accessible using this function. It's important to know the distinction between these two:\n\n- &#96;raw_user_meta_data&#96; - can be updated by the authenticated user using the &#96;supabase.auth.update()&#96; function. It is not a good place to store authorization data.\n- &#96;raw_app_meta_data&#96; - cannot be updated by the user, so it's a good place to store authorization data.\n\nThe &#96;auth.jwt()&#96; function is extremely versatile. For example, if you store some team data inside &#96;app_metadata&#96;, you can use it to determine whether a particular user belongs to a team. For example, if this was an array of IDs:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"User is in team\"\non my_table\nto authenticated\nusing ( team_id in (select auth.jwt() -&gt; 'app_metadata' -&gt; 'teams'));\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### MFA\n\nThe &#96;auth.jwt()&#96; function can be used to check for [Multi-Factor Authentication](mdc:docs/guides/auth/auth-mfa#enforce-rules-for-mfa-logins). For example, you could restrict a user from updating their profile unless they have at least 2 levels of authentication (Assurance Level 2):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Restrict updates.\"\non profiles\nas restrictive\nfor update\nto authenticated using (\n  (select auth.jwt()-&gt;&gt;'aal') = 'aal2'\n);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## RLS performance recommendations\n\nEvery authorization system has an impact on performance. While row level security is powerful, the performance impact is important to keep in mind. This is especially true for queries that scan every row in a table - like many &#96;select&#96; operations, including those using limit, offset, and ordering.\n\nBased on a series of [tests](mdc:https:/github.com/GaryAustin1/RLS-Performance), we have a few recommendations for RLS:\n\n### Add indexes\n\nMake sure you've added [indexes](mdc:docs/guides/database/postgres/indexes) on any columns used within the Policies which are not already indexed (or primary keys). For a Policy like this:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Users can access their own records\" on test_table",

        "contents": "- &#96;anon&#96;: an unauthenticated request (the user is not logged in)\n- &#96;authenticated&#96;: an authenticated request (the user is logged in)\n\nThese are actually [Postgres Roles](mdc:docs/guides/database/postgres/roles). You can use these roles within your Policies using the &#96;TO&#96; clause:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Profiles are viewable by everyone\"\non profiles\nfor select\nto authenticated, anon\nusing ( true );\n\n-- OR\n\ncreate policy \"Public profiles are viewable only by authenticated users\"\non profiles\nfor select\nto authenticated\nusing ( true );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nNote that &#96;for ...&#96; must be added after the table but before the roles. &#96;to ...&#96; must be added after &#96;for ...&#96;:\n\n### Incorrect\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Public profiles are viewable only by authenticated users\"\non profiles\nto authenticated\nfor select\nusing ( true );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Correct\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Public profiles are viewable only by authenticated users\"\non profiles\nfor select\nto authenticated\nusing ( true );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Multiple operations\n\nPostgreSQL policies do not support specifying multiple operations in a single FOR clause. You need to create separate policies for each operation.\n\n### Incorrect\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Profiles can be created and deleted by any user\"\non profiles\nfor insert, delete -- cannot create a policy on multiple operators\nto authenticated\nwith check ( true )\nusing ( true );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Correct\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate policy \"Profiles can be created by any user\"\non profiles\nfor insert\nto authenticated\nwith check ( true );\n\ncreate policy \"Profiles can be deleted by any user\"\non profiles\nfor delete\nto authenticated\nusing ( true );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Helper functions\n\nSupabase provides some helper functions that make it easier to write Policies.\n\n### &#96;auth.uid()&#96;\n\nReturns the ID of the user making the request.\n\n### &#96;auth.jwt()&#96;\n\nReturns the JWT of the user making the request. Anything that you store in the user's &#96;raw_app_meta_data&#96; column or the &#96;raw_user_meta_data&#96; column will be accessible using this function. It's important to know the distinction between these two:\n\n- &#96;raw_user_meta_data&#96; - can be updated by the authenticated user using the &#96;supabase.auth.update()&#96; function. It is not a good place to store authorization data.",

        "contents": "\"use client\";\n\nimport { useState, useEffect } from \"react\";\nimport { createClient } from \"@/lib/supabase/client\";\nimport { GoogleLoginButton } from \"@/components/google-login-button\";\nimport { Button } from \"@/components/ui/button\";\nimport { Input } from \"@/components/ui/input\";\nimport { Label } from \"@/components/ui/label\";\nimport {\n  Card,\n  CardContent,\n  CardDescription,\n  CardHeader,\n  CardTitle,\n} from \"@/components/ui/card\";\nimport { Badge } from \"@/components/ui/badge\";\n\n/**\n * Test page for verifying auth restrictions\n * Tests:\n * - Google OAuth signup (should work)\n * - Email/password signup (should be blocked)\n * - OTP email signup (should be blocked)\n * - Email identity addition (should validate CZU domain)\n */\nexport default function AuthTestPage() {\n  const [user, setUser] = useState&lt;any&gt;(null);\n  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true);\n  const [testResults, setTestResults] = useState&lt;{\n    emailPassword?: { success: boolean; message: string };\n    emailOTP?: { success: boolean; message: string };\n    emailIdentity?: { success: boolean; message: string };\n  }&gt;({});\n\n  const supabase = createClient();\n\n  useEffect(() =&gt; {\n    checkUser();\n    supabase.auth.onAuthStateChange(() =&gt; {\n      checkUser();\n    });\n  }, []);\n\n  const checkUser = async () =&gt; {\n    const {\n      data: { user: currentUser },\n    } = await supabase.auth.getUser();\n    setUser(currentUser);\n    setLoading(false);\n  };\n\n  const testEmailPasswordSignup = async (e: React.FormEvent&lt;HTMLFormElement&gt;)\n;\n}",

    {
      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./.cursor/plans/work_email_auth_system_467a2b18.plan.md",
        "range": {
          "startPosition": {
            "line": 251
          },
          "endPosition": {
            "line": 326
          }
        },
        "contents": "   - No Row Level Security policies\n   - No database triggers or functions\n   - All access control handled by Next.js\n\n### Next.js (Application Layer - All Business Logic)\n\n1. **Middleware Verification**:\n\n   - Queries &#96;profiles&#96; table for linked user_id\n   - Checks &#96;removed_access&#96; is null for active access\n   - Enforces role-based route protection\n   - Real-time verification (instant access revocation)\n\n2. **Domain Validation** (in server actions):\n\n   - Client-side validation for UX (immediate feedback)\n   - Server-side validation before sending OTP\n   - Validates email format and CZU domain\n\n3. **Access Management** (in server actions):\n\n   - Admin sets &#96;removed_access&#96; timestamp and &#96;removed_access_by&#96; profile\n   - Immediate effect on next request\n   - Audit trail of who revoked access and when\n\n## Authentication Flow Details\n\n### Step 1: Google Login\n\nUser clicks Google login button, Supabase handles OAuth flow.\n\n### Step 2: Work Email Input with Domain Validation\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// Validate domain before sending OTP\nif (!isValidWorkEmailDomain(workEmail)) {\n  throw new Error('Email must be @studenti.czu.cz or @pef.czu.cz');\n}\n\n// Send OTP to work email (only after domain validation passes)\nconst { error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithOtp({\n  email: workEmail,\n  options: { shouldCreateUser: false }\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Step 3: OTP Verification and Profile Linking\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// After user enters OTP, verify it\nconst { error } = await supabase.auth.verifyOtp({\n  email: workEmail,\n  token: otpCode,\n  type: 'email'\n});\n\n// Check if profile exists for this work email\nconst { data: profile } = await supabase\n  .from('profiles')\n  .select('id')\n  .eq('work_email', workEmail)\n  .single();\n\nif (!profile) {\n  // No profile exists - redirect to pending approval\n  redirect('/auth/pending-approval');\n}\n\n// Link profile to current user\nconst { data: { user } } = await supabase.auth.getUser();\nawait supabase\n  .from('profiles')\n  .update({ \n    user_id: user.id,",

        "contents": "import { redirect } from \"next/navigation\";\nimport { hasLinkedProfile } from \"@/lib/auth-helpers\";\n\n/**\n * Pending approval page\n * Shown to users who have verified their email but don't have a linked profile yet\n */\nexport default async function PendingApprovalPage() {\n  const supabase = await createClient();\n  const { data } = await supabase.auth.getClaims();\n\n  // Redirect to login if not authenticated\n  if (!data?.claims) {\n    redirect(\"/auth/login\");\n  }\n\n  // Redirect to protected if already has linked profile\n  const hasProfile = await hasLinkedProfile();\n  if (hasProfile) {\n    redirect(\"/protected\");\n  }\n\n  return (\n    &lt;div className=\"flex min-h-svh w-full items-center justify-center p-6 md:p-10\"&gt;\n      &lt;div className=\"w-full max-w-md\"&gt;\n        &lt;div className=\"flex flex-col gap-6\"&gt;\n          &lt;div className=\"flex flex-col gap-2\"&gt;\n            &lt;h1 className=\"text-2xl font-bold\"&gt;Pending Approval&lt;/h1&gt;\n            &lt;p className=\"text-muted-foreground\"&gt;\n              Your email address has been verified, but you need an admin to approve your account before you can access protected areas.\n            &lt;/p&gt;\n          &lt;/div&gt;\n          &lt;div className=\"rounded-lg border p-4 bg-muted/50\"&gt;\n            &lt;p className=\"text-sm\"&gt;\n              Please contact an administrator to approve your email address. Once approved, you will be able to access all protected areas of the application.\n            &lt;/p&gt;\n          &lt;/div&gt;\n        &lt;/div&gt;\n      &lt;/div&gt;\n    &lt;/div&gt;\n  );\n}",

        "contents": "import { cookies } from \"next/headers\";\n\n/**\n * Especially important if using Fluid compute: Don't put this client in a\n * global variable. Always create a new client within each function when using\n * it.\n */\nexport async function createClient() {\n  const cookieStore = await cookies();\n\n  return createServerClient(\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL!,\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY!,\n    {\n      cookies: {\n        getAll() {\n          return cookieStore.getAll();\n        },\n        setAll(cookiesToSet) {\n          try {\n            cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value, options }) =&gt;\n              cookieStore.set(name, value, options),\n            );\n          } catch {\n            // The &#96;setAll&#96; method was called from a Server Component.\n            // This can be ignored if you have proxy refreshing\n            // user sessions.\n          }\n        },\n      },\n    },\n  );\n}",

        "contents": "-- Migration: Initial schema setup\n-- Purpose: Creates complete database schema with tables, triggers, and restrictive RLS policies\n-- Affected tables: users, profiles, teams\n-- Special considerations: All RLS policies are restrictive - admin operations require service_role or application-level checks\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- ENUM TYPES\n-- ============================================================================\n\ncreate type public.profile_role as enum ('student', 'team_leader', 'coach', 'admin');\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- TABLES\n-- ============================================================================\n\n-- Create users table (custom table, separate from auth.users)\n-- Stores Google OAuth user data and OTP tracking\n-- Linked to auth.users via auth_user_id for authentication checks\ncreate table public.users (\n  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),\n  auth_user_id uuid unique references auth.users(id) on delete cascade,\n  google_email text not null unique,\n  suggested_work_email text,\n  google_profile_picture text,\n  google_full_name text,\n  last_otp_sent_at timestamptz,\n  created_at timestamptz default now() not null,\n  updated_at timestamptz default now() not null\n);\n\ncomment on table public.users is 'Custom users table storing Google OAuth user data and OTP tracking.         "contents": "-- Migration: Link users to profiles based on email matching\n-- Purpose: Automatically links profile rows to user rows when auth.users.email matches profiles.work_email\n-- Affected tables: profiles, users, auth.users\n-- Special considerations: Runs automatically when user email changes in auth.users table\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- FUNCTIONS\n-- ============================================================================\n\n-- Create trigger function to link profiles to users based on email matching\n-- Matches auth.users.email with profiles.work_email and links via public.users\n-- Runs with SECURITY DEFINER to access auth.users table\ncreate or replace function public.link_user_to_profile()\nreturns trigger\nlanguage plpgsql\nsecurity definer\nset search_path = public, auth\nas $$\ndeclare\n  v_user_id uuid;\n  v_auth_email text;\nbegin\n  -- Get the email from auth.users (use NEW.email after update)\n  v_auth_email := new.email;\n  \n  -- Only proceed if email is not null and has changed\n  if v_auth_email is null or v_auth_email = '' then\n    return new;\n  end if;\n  \n  -- Find the public.users row that matches this auth.users.id\n  select id into v_user_id\n  from public.users\n  where auth_user_id = new.id;\n  \n  -- If no matching public.users row found, return early\n  if v_user_id is null then\n    return new;\n  end if;\n  \n  -- Link profile to user if work_email matches auth.users.email\n  -- Only update if profile exists and is not already linked to a different user\n  update public.profiles\n  set user_id = v_user_id\n  where work_email = lower(trim(v_auth_email))\n    and (user_id is null or user_id = v_user_id);\n  \n  return new;\nend;\n$$;\n\ncomment on function public.link_user_to_profile() is 'Trigger function that automatically links profile rows to user rows when auth.users.email matches profiles.work_email. Matches based on currently logged in user email (auth.users.email), uid in user table row (public.users.auth_user_id), and work_email in profile table row (public.profiles.work_email).';\n\n-- ============================================================================",

        "contents": "create table public.profiles (\n  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),\n  name text not null,\n  picture text,\n  user_id uuid unique references public.users(id) on delete set null,\n  work_email text unique not null,\n  role public.profile_role not null default 'student',\n  team_id uuid references public.teams(id) on delete set null,\n  phone_number text,\n  personal_email text,\n  date_of_birth date,\n  removed_access timestamptz,\n  removed_access_by uuid references public.profiles(id) on delete set null,\n  created_at timestamptz default now() not null,\n  updated_at timestamptz default now() not null,\n  constraint valid_czu_domain check (\n    work_email like '%@studenti.czu.cz' or work_email like '%@pef.czu.cz'\n  )\n);\n\ncomment on table public.profiles is 'User profile data with role and team membership. Pre-created by admin, linked to user after OTP verification.';\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- FUNCTIONS\n-- ============================================================================\n\n-- Create trigger function to automatically update updated_at column\ncreate or replace function public.handle_updated_at()\nreturns trigger\nlanguage plpgsql\nsecurity invoker\nset search_path = ''\nas $$\nbegin\n  new.updated_at := now();\n  return new;\nend;\n$$;\n\ncomment on function public.handle_updated_at() is 'Trigger function that automatically updates the updated_at column to the current timestamp on row updates.';\n\n-- Create trigger function to populate public.users on auth.users creation\n-- Extracts Google OAuth data from auth.users.raw_user_meta_data and auth.users.email\ncreate or replace function public.handle_new_auth_user()\nreturns trigger\nlanguage plpgsql\nsecurity definer\nset search_path = public, auth\nas $$\ndeclare\n  v_google_email text;\n  v_google_full_name text;\n  v_google_profile_picture text;\n  v_raw_meta_data jsonb;\nbegin\n  v_raw_meta_data := new.raw_user_meta_data;",

        "contents": "await supabase\n  .from('profiles')\n  .update({ \n    user_id: user.id,\n    picture: user.user_metadata.avatar_url  // Default to Google picture\n  })\n  .eq('work_email', workEmail);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Step 4: Middleware Validation\n\nQuery database for profile linked to current auth.user and check &#96;removed_access IS NULL&#96; on every request to protected routes.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// Middleware check\nconst { data: profile } = await supabase\n  .from('profiles')\n  .select('id, role, removed_access')\n  .eq('user_id', user.id)\n  .single();\n\nif (!profile) redirect('/auth/verify-work-email');\nif (profile.removed_access) redirect('/auth/access-revoked');\n// User has active access, continue...\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Estimated Complexity\n\n| Task | Complexity | Lines of Code |\n\n|------|------------|---------------|\n\n| Delete old auth files | Trivial | -500 lines |\n\n| Security lockdown config | Trivial | ~20 lines TOML |\n\n| Database migration | Low | ~40 lines SQL (users, profiles, indexes) |\n\n| Constants + validation | Trivial | ~25 lines |\n\n| Server actions (auth logic) | Medium | ~60 lines |\n\n| Middleware update | Medium | ~50 lines (includes DB queries) |\n\n| Google login page | Low | ~30 lines |\n\n| Work email form + linking | Medium | ~120 lines |\n\n| Pending approval page | Low | ~20 lines |\n\n| Access revoked page | Low | ~20 lines |\n\n**Total new code**: ~385 lines (vs ~500 lines deleted)\n\n## Separation of Concerns\n\n### Supabase (Auth + Storage Only)\n\n- **Authentication**: Google OAuth flow, session management, OTP emails\n- **Database**: Store profiles and users data (no RLS - Next.js handles access control)\n- **No business logic**: No custom hooks, no stored procedures, no triggers, no functions\n\n### Next.js (All Business Logic)\n\n- **Middleware**: Profile verification, access checks, role-based routing\n- **Server Actions**: Profile linking, access revocation\n- **Validation**: Domain validation, input sanitization, business rules\n- **Authorization**: Role hierarchy checks, permission enforcement\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                         Next.js                                  │",

        "contents": "export async function updateSession(request: NextRequest) {\n\n\n  // Redirect to login if not authenticated (except for public routes)\n  if (!isPublicRoute &amp;&amp; !user) {\n    const url = request.nextUrl.clone();\n    url.pathname = \"/auth/login\";\n    return NextResponse.redirect(url);\n  }\n\n  // Check for linked profile if user is authenticated and not on public routes\n  if (user &amp;&amp; !isPublicRoute) {\n    // Get the public.users row linked to this auth user\n    const { data: publicUser } = await supabase\n      .from(\"users\")\n      .select(\"id\")\n      .eq(\"auth_user_id\", user.sub)\n      .single();\n\n    // If no publicUser or no linked profile, redirect to pending approval\n    if (!publicUser) {\n      const url = request.nextUrl.clone();\n      url.pathname = \"/auth/pending-approval\";\n      return NextResponse.redirect(url);\n    }\n\n    // Check if there's a profile linked to this user\n    const { data: profile } = await supabase\n      .from(\"profiles\")\n      .select(\"id\")\n      .eq(\"user_id\", publicUser.id)\n      .single();\n\n    if (!profile) {\n      // User doesn't have a linked profile, redirect to pending approval\n      const url = request.nextUrl.clone();\n      url.pathname = \"/auth/pending-approval\";\n      return NextResponse.redirect(url);\n    }\n  }\n\n  // IMPORTANT: You *must* return the supabaseResponse object as it is.\n  // If you're creating a new response object with NextResponse.next() make sure to:\n  // 1. Pass the request in it, like so:\n  //    const myNewResponse = NextResponse.next({ request })\n  // 2. Copy over the cookies, like so:\n  //    myNewResponse.cookies.setAll(supabaseResponse.cookies.getAll())\n  // 3. Finally:\n  //    return myNewResponse\n  // If this is not done, you may be causing the browser and server to go out\n  // of sync and terminate the user's session prematurely!\n\n  return supabaseResponse;\n}",

        "contents": "import { redirect } from \"next/navigation\";\nimport { type NextRequest } from \"next/server\";\n\nimport { hasEmailIdentity } from \"@/lib/auth-helpers\";\n\n/**\n * Handles OAuth callback from Google\n * Exchanges the code for a session and redirects appropriately\n */\nexport async function GET(request: NextRequest) {\n  const { searchParams, origin } = new URL(request.url);\n  const code = searchParams.get(\"code\");\n  const next = searchParams.get(\"next\");\n\n  if (code) {\n    const supabase = await createClient();\n    const { error } = await supabase.auth.exchangeCodeForSession(code);\n\n    if (!error) {\n      // Check if user has email identity linked\n      // If not, redirect to verify-email page\n      const hasEmail = await hasEmailIdentity();\n      const redirectTo = next || (hasEmail ? \"/protected\" : \"/auth/verify-email\");\n      redirect(redirectTo);\n    }\n  }\n\n  // Redirect to error page if something went wrong\n  redirect(&#96;/auth/error?error=Failed to authenticate with Google&#96;);\n}",

        "contents": "└─ e2e/                       # End-to-end tests\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Directory Conventions\n\n- Use **kebab-case** for folders and files\n- Co-locate tests next to source: &#96;*.test.ts(x)&#96;\n- Export from &#96;index.ts&#96; barrels only when it helps DX without circular deps\n\n## Next.js App Router Rules\n\n### Server vs Client Components\n\n- **Default to RSC** (no \"use client\"). Use client components only for:\n  - Interactivity (event handlers)\n  - Browser APIs (localStorage, window, etc.)\n  - Third-party libraries requiring client-side initialization\n\n### Server Boundaries\n\n- Keep data access in server context (RSC, server actions, API routes)\n- API routes in &#96;app/api&#96; are for external webhooks only\n- Use internal APIs (tRPC, server actions) for app-to-app communication\n\n### Performance &amp; UX\n\n- Use &#96;&lt;Suspense&gt;&#96; for async UI; provide skeletons\n- Implement proper loading and error boundaries\n- Use Next.js caching (&#96;revalidateTag&#96;, &#96;revalidatePath&#96;) appropriately\n- Prefer Edge runtime for simple operations, Node for complex ones\n\n### Accessibility\n\n- All interactive elements must have proper roles and labels\n- Ensure keyboard navigation support\n- Provide ARIA attributes where needed\n- Test with screen readers\n\n## API Architecture\n\n### Internal APIs (tRPC Recommended)\n\n- Organize by feature domains\n- Use Zod for input validation\n- Implement proper error handling with custom error classes\n- Keep business logic server-side (no JSX in API layer)\n- Write integration tests with mocked external services\n- **Router logic should be application code only** - delegate to business logic services\n- **Use only protected procedures** for all endpoints\n- **Split procedures and routers** into separate files for better organization\n\n### Application Logic vs Business Logic\n\n**Application Logic** (in tRPC procedures):\n- Input validation and sanitization\n- Authentication and authorization checks\n- Request/response formatting\n- Error handling and mapping\n- Delegation to business logic services\n- Logging and observability",

        "contents": "---\nalwaysApply: true\ndescription: NextJs development rules\n---\n\n# Next.js Development Rules\n\nYou are an expert full-stack TypeScript engineer working with Next.js. Produce production-ready code that follows modern Next.js App Router patterns and best practices.\n\n## Tech Stack Guidelines\n\n- **Next.js 15+** (App Router) + React 19\n- **TypeScript** (strict mode)\n- **Testing**: Vitest + React Testing Library + MSW\n- **Styling**: Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui (when applicable)\n- **Package Manager**: pnpm\n\nFocus on: separation of concerns, strict typing, accessibility, performance, and comprehensive testing.\n\n## Project Structure\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nsrc/\n├─ app/                       # App Router (RSC by default)\n│  ├─ _components/            # App-level (RSC-ok) components\n│  ├─ api/                    # API routes for external webhooks only\n│  ├─ (routes)/               # Route groups and pages\n│  └─ layout.tsx\n├─ components/                # Reusable client/RSC components\n│  ├─ ui/                     # Base UI components\n│  └─ [feature]/              # Feature-specific components\n├─ lib/                       # Utilities and shared helpers\n├─ server/                    # Server-side code\n│  ├─ api/                    # tRPC API layer\n│  │  ├─ routers/             # tRPC router composition\n│  │  ├─ procedures/          # Individual tRPC procedures\n│  │  ├─ root.ts              # Root router\n│  │  └─ trpc.ts              # tRPC setup\n│  ├─ services/               # Business logic services\n│  └─ clients/                # External service clients\n├─ db/                        # Database schema &amp; migrations\n├─ tools/                     # AI tool definitions\n├─ prompts/                   # AI prompt templates\n└─ trpc/                      # tRPC client setup\n\ntest/\n├─ unit/                      # Unit tests\n├─ integ/                     # Integration tests\n└─ e2e/                       # End-to-end tests\n&#96;&#96;&#96;",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "---",
            "lineNumber": 1
          },
          {
            "text": "alwaysApply: true",
            "lineNumber": 2
          },
          {
            "text": "description: NextJs development rules",
            "lineNumber": 3
          },
          {
            "text": "---",
            "lineNumber": 4
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 5
          },
          {
            "text": "# Next.js Development Rules",
            "lineNumber": 6
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 7
          },
          {
            "text": "You are an expert full-stack TypeScript engineer working with Next.js. Produce production-ready code that follows modern Next.js App Router patterns and best practices.",
            "lineNumber": 8
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 9
          },
          {
            "text": "## Tech Stack Guidelines",
            "lineNumber": 10
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 11
          },
          {
            "text": "- **Next.js 15+** (App Router) + React 19",
            "lineNumber": 12
          },
          {

    {
      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./supabase/config.toml",
        "range": {
          "startPosition": {
            "line": 107
          },
          "endPosition": {
            "line": 170
          }

        "contents": "file_size_limit = \"50MiB\"\n\n# Uncomment to configure local storage buckets\n# [storage.buckets.images]\n# public = false\n# file_size_limit = \"50MiB\"\n# allowed_mime_types = [\"image/png\", \"image/jpeg\"]\n# objects_path = \"./images\"\n\n# Allow connections via S3 compatible clients\n[storage.s3_protocol]\nenabled = true\n\n# Image transformation API is available to Supabase Pro plan.\n# [storage.image_transformation]\n# enabled = true\n\n# Store analytical data in S3 for running ETL jobs over Iceberg Catalog\n# This feature is only available on the hosted platform.\n[storage.analytics]\nenabled = false\nmax_namespaces = 5\nmax_tables = 10\nmax_catalogs = 2\n\n# Analytics Buckets is available to Supabase Pro plan.\n# [storage.analytics.buckets.my-warehouse]\n\n# Store vector embeddings in S3 for large and durable datasets\n# This feature is only available on the hosted platform.\n[storage.vector]\nenabled = false\nmax_buckets = 10\nmax_indexes = 5\n\n# Vector Buckets is available to Supabase Pro plan.\n# [storage.vector.buckets.documents-openai]\n\n[auth]\nenabled = true\n# The base URL of your website.         "contents": "### ORM Best Practices\n\n- Use type-safe ORMs (Drizzle, Prisma, etc.)\n- Define schemas with proper relationships and constraints\n- Infer types from schema definitions\n- Write repository-style helpers to isolate queries\n- Implement proper migrations\n\n### Data Access Patterns\n\n- Keep database queries in dedicated modules\n- Avoid N+1 queries; use joins and CTEs\n- Implement pagination for list endpoints\n- Use select projections to limit payload size\n\n## Authentication &amp; Authorization\n\n- Implement server-side auth checks\n- Never trust client-side auth flags\n- Use middleware for route protection\n- Store user data securely with proper encryption\n\n## Testing Strategy\n\n### Unit Testing (Vitest)\n\n- **Never mock internal code** - only mock external dependencies\n- Use MSW for API mocking when needed\n- Test utilities, repositories, and business logic\n- Mock external services (APIs, databases, file systems)\n\n### Component Testing (React Testing Library)\n\n- Test interactive components with proper accessibility\n- Ensure loading and error states are covered\n- Test user interactions and state changes\n- Use data-testid sparingly; prefer semantic queries\n\n### Integration Testing\n\n- Test API endpoints with real database connections\n- Use test databases with proper cleanup\n- Test authentication flows end-to-end\n- Mock external services consistently\n\n### Test Structure\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// Example test structure\ndescribe(\"Feature\", () =&gt; {\n  describe(\"when condition\", () =&gt; {\n    it(\"should expected behavior\", async () =&gt; {\n      // Arrange\n      // Act\n      // Assert\n    });\n  });\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Error Handling &amp; Observability\n\n- Implement early returns on invalid input (fail fast)\n- Use typed error codes and messages\n- Log server-side with contextual metadata\n- Never expose stack traces to clients\n- Provide user-friendly error messages\n\n## Security Best Practices\n\n- Validate all inputs at boundaries\n- Use environment variables for sensitive data (server-only)\n- Implement proper CORS policies\n- Sanitize user inputs\n- Use HTTPS in production\n- Implement rate limiting where appropriate",

        "contents": "   - No Row Level Security policies\n   - No database triggers or functions\n   - All access control handled by Next.js\n\n### Next.js (Application Layer - All Business Logic)\n\n1. **Middleware Verification**:\n\n   - Queries &#96;profiles&#96; table for linked user_id\n   - Checks &#96;removed_access&#96; is null for active access\n   - Enforces role-based route protection\n   - Real-time verification (instant access revocation)\n\n2. **Domain Validation** (in server actions):\n\n   - Client-side validation for UX (immediate feedback)\n   - Server-side validation before sending OTP\n   - Validates email format and CZU domain\n\n3. **Access Management** (in server actions):\n\n   - Admin sets &#96;removed_access&#96; timestamp and &#96;removed_access_by&#96; profile\n   - Immediate effect on next request\n   - Audit trail of who revoked access and when\n\n## Authentication Flow Details\n\n### Step 1: Google Login\n\nUser clicks Google login button, Supabase handles OAuth flow.\n\n### Step 2: Work Email Input with Domain Validation\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// Validate domain before sending OTP\nif (!isValidWorkEmailDomain(workEmail)) {\n  throw new Error('Email must be @studenti.czu.cz or @pef.czu.cz');\n}\n\n// Send OTP to work email (only after domain validation passes)\nconst { error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithOtp({\n  email: workEmail,\n  options: { shouldCreateUser: false }\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Step 3: OTP Verification and Profile Linking\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// After user enters OTP, verify it\nconst { error } = await supabase.auth.verifyOtp({\n  email: workEmail,\n  token: otpCode,\n  type: 'email'\n});\n\n// Check if profile exists for this work email\nconst { data: profile } = await supabase\n  .from('profiles')\n  .select('id')\n  .eq('work_email', workEmail)\n  .single();\n\nif (!profile) {\n  // No profile exists - redirect to pending approval\n  redirect('/auth/pending-approval');\n}\n\n// Link profile to current user\nconst { data: { user } } = await supabase.auth.getUser();\nawait supabase\n  .from('profiles')\n  .update({ \n    user_id: user.id,",
